reflection_text.5:
The Stokes biharmonic solution for the $\sin kx$ mode can be written with
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $u_z=-kF\cos kx$, $(D^2-k^2)^2F=0$.
With $F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$ and the free-surface
kinematic/ no-slip conditions $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$ for the steady material
surface $w(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$ we have $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and up to an
inessential constant $F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$.
With the Stokes sign $\sigma_{ij}=-p\delta_{ij}+\mu(\partial_i u_j+\partial_ju_i)$

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^2F]\sin kx$, 
$P(z)=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^2F']$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu kF']\cos kx$,
and for the $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ branch

$P(z)=-2\mu k[d\sinh kz+b\cosh kz]$,
$P(0)=-2\mu k b$, $F'''(0)=2bk^2$,

so that on the free surface $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx=
\rho g e\cos kx$ and in the steady limit $\rho g e_s=2\mu k b$.

The base conditions stated in the problem are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, i.e.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu kF'(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^2F'(h)$,
$\mu[F''(h)+k^2F(h)]=S_0$.

With $u=kh$, $C_h=\cosh u$, $S_h=\sinh u$ this gives

$b[C_h-uS_h]=duC_h$,  $S_0/\mu=2k\big[(d+bu)C_h+udS_h\big]$,

whence

$b=\dfrac{S_0}{2\mu k}\dfrac{uC_h}{u^{2}+C_h^{2}},\qquad
d=b\,\dfrac{C_h-uS_h}{uC_h}$,

and

$\rho g e_s=2\mu k b=S_0\,\dfrac{uC_h}{u^{2}+C_h^{2}}$.

In modulus with the buoyancy contrast $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_s=\chi(u)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\displaystyle
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad u=kh$,

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^3)$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$ for $u\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\approx0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\approx1.0\!-\!1.2$, and the
geologically quoted $kh=O(1)$ estimate $\chi\approx1/2$,
$e_s\simeq\frac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$. The $90^{\circ}$ phase
$e_s\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$ is absorbed in the sign.

Disagreement in the deliberation is the extra base condition.
Colleague 2/7 impose the additional impermeability $F(h)=0$, i.e.
$\Phi(h)=0$, which gives the compact transfer

$\chi_0(u)=u/[C_h+uS_h]$,
$e_s=S_0/(\Delta\rho g)\,kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$,

$\chi_0\simeq u$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi_{0\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$.
This is the same physics with $F(h)=0$ and coincides with $\chi_A$
to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ but is not identical at $O(1)$.

Colleague 4/6 retain the $2\mu w_z$ term in an alternative bookkeeping
and obtain the sinh-numerator form
$\chi_s(u)=uS_h/[u^{2}+C_h^{2}]$, i.e. $e_s\propto kh\sinh kh/[\cosh^2kh+(kh)^2]$,
which gives $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$, inconsistent with the
lubrication expectation $\chi\sim u$ for a finite-thickness viscous
sheet with the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$ conditions.

With the problem statement as written – $u_x(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$, no imposed $w(h)=0$ – the $F(0)=F'(0)=0$ solution above, i.e. $\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$, is the correct steady Stokes transfer function. In the usual $kh\sim O(1)$ geophysical normalisation this is quoted as the familiar $O(1/2)$ dynamic-topography factor, essentially $e_s\approx\frac12 S_0/\Delta\rho g$. The $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ form is the same response under the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$.
reflection_text.2:
The stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$.
With the material steady free surface $z=0$

$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0\iff u_{x}(0)=0,\;w(0)=0$,

$\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,

$\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2}$ so that

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e_{s}$,
$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$,

and

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.

With $u=kh$, $C_{u}=\cosh u$, $S_{u}=\sinh u$,

$\Phi'(h)=DkuC_{u}+(Bu+D)S_{u}$,
$\Phi'''(h)=k^{2}\big[3DS_{u}+2BC_{u}+DuC_{u}+BuS_{u}\big]$

gives $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)\iff B(C_{u}-uS_{u})=DuC_{u}$,
$D=B(C_{u}-uS_{u})/(uC_{u})$, and

$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[C_{u}(Bu+D)+DuS_{u}\big]
=2kB\frac{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}{uC_{u}}$.

Hence

$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2kB\frac{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}{uC_{u}}$,
$\displaystyle B=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\frac{uC_{u}}{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}$,

and on the steady branch

$\displaystyle\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kB
=S_{0}\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}$,
$u=kh$.

In modulus, with the buoyancy contrast $\Delta\rho$ normally used for
dynamic topography,

$e_{s}=\chi(kh)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\displaystyle\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
=\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

$e_{s}\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, the $90^{\circ}$ phase
being absorbed in sign.  $\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$, 
$\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$ for $u\gg1$, 
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$, so that for the
geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{0}\approx\frac12$,
the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography, with the long-wave
lubrication limit $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The form $\chi_{B}(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ quoted by Colleagues 2 and 7
is the $F(h)=0$ impermeable-base normalisation, i.e. $W(h)=0$ imposed
in addition to $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  With the four conditions stated in
the problem, $\Phi(h)=0$ is not required and the impermeable
normalisation changes the denominator.  The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$
sinh-numerator form of Colleagues 4 and 6 gives $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for
$u\ll1$, inconsistent with the lubrication expectation $e_{s}\propto kh$,
and is a double counting of the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term after $W'(0)=0$ has
already been used.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the usual
buoyancy renormalisation; with $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the above $\chi$
is the conventional $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ transfer function,
often quoted in the $kh\sim1$ limit as $\chi\approx1/2$. ∎
reflection_text.3:
The steady 2-D Stokes problem can be written with the stream function
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $D=d/dz$.  With the usual Stokes sign
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\,[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[F'''-3k^{2}F']\cos kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$,
the top conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$
give $F'(0)=0$, $\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e$.  The base
conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$, and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$.
With the $ \sin kx$ mode $F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$,
$F'(0)=0$ gives $b+kc=0$ and, up to an inessential additive constant,
$F(z)=-kc\,z\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$.  Then
$F'''(0)=-2k^{3}c$, so that with the buoyancy contrast
$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= -2\mu k^{2}c$.
The zero normal traction at the base $F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ gives
$c+dh=kc\,h\tanh kh$.  Imposing
$\mu[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)]=S_{0}$ eliminates $d$ and yields
$2\mu k^{2}c\,$[ $-\,c_{h}^{2}-u^{2}]/\,u\,c_{h}=S_{0}$,
$c_{h}=\cosh u$, $u=kh$, i.e.
$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,u\,c_{h}/(u^{2}+c_{h}^{2})$.
In modulus, with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase absorbed in the sign,
\[
e_{s}= \chi(u)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
      =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad u=kh .
\]
Hence $\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$ for
$u\gg1$, with $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$.
For the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$ mode this is the familiar
viscous-isostatic dynamic-topography factor
$e_{s}\simeq \tfrac12\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $\chi_{0}\approx1/2$,
and the long-wave lubrication limit $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ form,
$\chi_{B}=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$, is the same physics obtained with the
conventional impermeable-base normalisation $F(h)=0$, i.e. with
$P(h)=0$ instead of the full $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, and coincides with
$\chi_{A}$ to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$.  The sinh-numerator form
$\chi_{C}=u\sinh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ gives the incorrect
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ long-wave limit and is ruled out on asymptotic
grounds.  The double counting of the $2\mu w_{z}$ viscous normal stress
at the free surface after $w_{z}(0)=0$ has already been imposed by
$u_{x}(0)=0$ is the source of the $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ vs
$u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ discrepancy discussed by Colleagues 4,6,7.
With the statement $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ the consistent transfer function
is the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ screening quoted above, and the
usual geophysical $O(1)$ estimate is $\chi\approx1/2$ for $kh\sim1$, up
to the conventional $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ renormalisation.

2.text:
With the harmonic mode

$$
\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$ \nabla^{4}\psi =0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with
$\sigma_{ij}=-p\delta_{ij}+2\mu e_{ij}$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\Big[\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad p=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] .
$$

On the material steady free surface

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad w(0)=0\Longleftrightarrow 
\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that up to an additive constant

$$
\Phi(z)=b\,z\cosh kz +\big(c+dz\big)\sinh kz ,\qquad 
c=-\frac{b}{k},
$$

and $w_{,z}(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-p(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
            =2\mu k\,b\cos kx .
$$

Hence on the steady branch, with the buoyancy renormalisation
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k\,b,\qquad 
e_{s}\propto\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$
being absorbed in the sign.

At the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\tag{1}
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}. \tag{2}
$$

Put $u=kh$, $C_{u}=\cosh u$, $S_{u}=\sinh u$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi'(h)=Dk uC_{u}+(Bu+D)S_{u},\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)=k^{2}\!\Big[3DS_{u}+2BC_{u}+DuC_{u}+BuS_{u}\Big],
$$

where $B=b$, $D=d$.  Condition (1) is

$$
B\big[C_{u}-uS_{u}\big]=DuC_{u},
\qquad 
D=B\frac{C_{u}-uS_{u}}{uC_{u}} .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\Big[C_{u}(Bu+D)+DuS_{u}\Big]
       =2kB\frac{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}{uC_{u}} .
$$

Hence from (2)

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2kB\frac{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}{uC_{u}},\qquad
B=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\frac{uC_{u}}{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}} .
$$

With $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kB$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},\qquad u=kh,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
      =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
$$

the sign being the usual $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$
phase shift.  In particular

$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1,\qquad 
\chi(u)\sim2u\,e^{-u}\to0,\;u\gg1,
$$

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47\quad{\rm at}\quad kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}\approx \tfrac12,
$$

the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography.  The long-wave
lubrication limit is $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and the exponential screening for $kh\gg1$ is obtained.  The
$u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ form is the same response with the additional
impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$ imposed in
addition to the four conditions quoted in the statement; with the
four stated conditions $\Phi(h)=0$ is not required and the transfer
function above is the conventional $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ viscous
isostatic response, often quoted as $e_{s}\approx \tfrac12\,
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\sim1$.  Up to sign this is the $e_{s}\propto
S_{0}$ steady dynamic topography with the $90^{\circ}$ phase between
basal shear $\sin kx$ and surface topography $\cos kx$. ∎

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the bookkeeping of the viscous normal stress at the free surface is the point where the different algebraic forms diverge, and it is worth re-checking it very carefully.

With the stream function $\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, the Stokes stresses are
\[
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=\Big[\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx
          =-P+2\mu w_{,z},
\]
with $P=-(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.
The steady material free surface is
\[
w(0)=0,\qquad u_x(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0 .
\]
Hence $w_{,z}(0)=-k\Phi'(0)=0$ identically, so that on the top
\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
\]
The $2\mu w_{,z}$ viscous normal stress is already zero by $u_x(0)=0$; it should not be kept as an independent contribution after the kinematic condition is imposed. With $\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,
\[
\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx .
\]
With the buoyancy condition $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_s\cos kx$,
\[
\Delta\rho g e_s =2\mu k b, \tag{1}
\]
so the surface topography is fixed by the single constant $b$ and there is no residual $2\mu W'(0)$ term to carry through the elimination.

At the base
\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h), \tag{2}
\]
i.e. $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$, and the imposed shear
\[
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_0 . \tag{3}
\]
Writing $u=kh$, $c_h=\cosh u$, $s_h=\sinh u$,
\[
\Phi'(h)=dkh\,c_h+(bkh+d)s_h .
\]
Eq.(2) is
\[
b\big[c_h-u s_h\big]=d\,u c_h , \tag{4}
\]
and
\[
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)c_h+ud s_h\big].
\]
Eliminating $d$ with (4) in (3) gives
\[
\frac{S_0}{\mu}=2k b\big[c_h+u s_h\big],
\]
so that
\[
b=\frac{S_0}{2k\mu}\frac{1}{c_h+u s_h}.
\]
With (1)
\[
\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k b=\frac{S_0\,u}{c_h+u s_h},
\]
up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase. In modulus
\[
e_s=\chi(u)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u},\qquad u=kh,
\]
i.e. $\chi(u)=\big[u/\cosh u+\cosh u/u\big]^{-1}$ on the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$ which removes the additive constant in the biharmonic solution.

This gives the expected asymptotics
\[
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1,\qquad 
\chi(u)\to0,\;u\gg1,
\]
with $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, the familiar $O(1/2)$ viscous-isostatic value for $kh=O(1)$ and the linear lubrication limit $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ form that appears in 1,3,5 is obtained if the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term is kept symbolically in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu w_{,z}(0)$ after $w_{,z}(0)=0$ has already been imposed by $u_x(0)=0$, and then $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ is used together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two independent conditions. Once $W'(0)=0$ is enforced, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly and the extra $2\mu W'$ is already absorbed; retaining it a second time in the elimination produces the additional $\cosh^{2}u$ term in the denominator. The two expressions coincide only to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi\sim kh$, which is why the long-wave lubrication limit is the same in both camps.

The $u\sinh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ sinh-numerator form gives $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$, a quadratic long-wave limit inconsistent with the lubrication expectation for a finite thickness viscous sheet, and can be discarded on asymptotic grounds.

With the usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy renormalisation this is the compact steady transfer function most commonly quoted for a viscous sheet with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$ and the $90^{\circ}$ phase between basal shear $\sin kx$ and surface topography $\cos kx$.

1.text:
With the $\sin kx$ mode put
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$, $D=d/dz$,

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big]$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\big[-P-2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx
          =\mu k^{-1}\big[F'''-3k^{2}F'\big]\cos kx$.

In the steady material limit $w(0)=u_{x}(0)=0$,

$F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0$,

so that with an inessential constant removed

$F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $b=-kc$,

$F'(0)=0$, $w_{z}(0)=0$.
Then

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$, 
$F'''(0)=2k^{2}b$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
\qquad b=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{2\mu k}\;,
\tag{1}
$$
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being absorbed in the sign.

At $z=h$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,

i.e. with $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$,

$C_{h}\big[b-ku d\big]=2S_{h}\big[d+ku b\big]$,
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\Big[C_{h}\big(d+k b h\big)+k d hS_{h}\Big]$ .

With $b=-kc$ the normal-traction condition gives
$d=c\,u^{-1}\big[u\tanh u-1\big]$ and after elimination of $d$

$$
\mu\,2k\Big\{d\big[C_{h}+uS_{h}\big]-k^{2}c\,h C_{h}\Big\}=S_{0},
$$

i.e.

$$
c=-\frac{S_{0}h^{2}C_{h}}{2\mu u\big[u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\big]},\qquad
b=-kc=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\frac{uC_{h}}{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}} .
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b
   =S_{0}\,\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},\qquad u=kh,
$$

so that in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad u=kh,
$$

$e_{s}\propto\cos kx$ against $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, the usual
$90^{\circ}$ phase shift.  In particular

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\to0$,  $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0,\;u\to\infty$,

$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45-0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0-1.2$,

and for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}\approx\frac12 ,
$$

i.e. the familiar viscous-isostatic
$e_{s}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$ dynamic topography, the $-$ sign
being the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase.  In the long wave
lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ so that $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

With the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$,
$W(h)=0$, the same stream function is usually written in the compact
form $\chi_{0}(u)=u\big[\cosh u+u\sinh u\big]^{-1}$, which coincides
with the expression above to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and gives
$\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$.  The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$
numerator is obtained by double counting the $2\mu w_{z}$ viscous normal
stress after $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ has already been used and gives the
wrong quadratic long-wave limit $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$.  The $u\cosh u/
[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ screening is the steady Stokes response to
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under the stated conditions
$F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, and reduces to the quoted
$\chi\approx1/2$ for $kh\sim O(1)$. ∎

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think we are now close on the common denominator $u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u$ and the only remaining physical point is the way the normal traction is closed at the two boundaries.

Put $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with the usual Stokes sign
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= [\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.  
The steady material free surface is
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ so that $w_{,z}(0)=0$ identically.
Hence
\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx,
\qquad\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2},
\]
and with the normalisation $\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,
\[
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b,
\tag{1}
\]
the $2\mu w_{,z}$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ being identically zero at $z=0$
once $u_{x}(0)=0$ is imposed. There is therefore no independent
$2\mu W'(0)$ contribution to keep at the top; $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$
exactly.

At the base the problem states $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, not $P(h)=0$.  With
$w_{,z}=-k\Phi'$,
\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff -P(h)+2\mu w_{,z}(h)=0\iff
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),
\tag{2}
\]
i.e. $U''-3k^{2}U=0$ for $U=\Phi'$.  This is the physical coupling of
pressure and viscous normal stress at the asthenosphere interface.
With $u=kh$, $c_{h}=\cosh u$, $s_{h}=\sinh u$,
\[
\Phi'(h)=dkh c_{h}+(bh+d)s_{h},\qquad
b[c_{h}-u s_{h}]=d\,u c_{h},
\tag{3}
\]
which is (2). The imposed basal shear is
\[
\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0},
\tag{4}
\]
and
\[
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)c_{h}+ud\,s_{h}\big].
\]
Eliminating $d$ with (3) in (4) gives
\[
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\,
\frac{u\,s_{h}\big[c_{h}^{2}+u^{2}\big]+u^{2}c_{h}s_{h}}{c_{h}^{2}+u^{2}}
=2k b\,\frac{u s_{h}}{c_{h}^{2}+u^{2}}\,
\Big[c_{h}^{2}+u^{2}+u\,c_{h}s_{h}\Big],
\]
and using (3) to replace the bracket one obtains the closed form
\[
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\,
\frac{u\,s_{h}}{u^{2}+c_{h}^{2}} .
\]
With (1)
\[
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b
   =S_{0}\,\frac{u\sinh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},
\qquad u=kh,
\]
up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$,
i.e. in modulus
\[
e_{s}= \chi(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u\,\sinh u}{\cosh^{2}u+u^{2}} .
\]
This is the transfer function that follows from the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu w_{,z}$ at both boundaries with the free-surface
kinematic conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and the physical base condition
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  In particular
\[
\chi(u)=\frac{u^{2}}{2}+O(u^{4}),\;u\ll1,\qquad
\chi(u)\sim u e^{-u},\;u\gg1,
\]
so the exponential screening for $kh\gg1$ is recovered and the long-wave
lubrication screening is quadratic, as it must be when the viscous normal
stress $2\mu w_{,z}$ is retained at the base through (2).

The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ form of Colleagues 1,3,5 is obtained if
the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term is dropped at the base, i.e. if $P(h)=0$ is used
instead of $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, or equivalently if the $2\mu W'$ contribution
is kept a second time after $W'(0)=0$ has already been imposed by
$u_{x}(0)=0$.  That is the double counting that Colleague 4 has been
pointing out: once $W'(0)=0$ the free-surface normal traction is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly, and re-introducing an effective
$2\mu W'$ in the elimination produces the extra $\cosh$ factor in the
numerator.

The compact form $\chi_{0}=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ that Colleague 4 now
writes down is the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ result after the
additional impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$ is imposed.  The two
expressions coincide only to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$, which is why Colleague 2’s
claim of algebraic equivalence between
$u\cosh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ and $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ cannot hold
exactly.  The minimal, physically consistent set
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives the
$\sinh$-numerator transfer function above, with the familiar
$O(1/2)$ geophysical value for $kh\sim O(1)$ and the required $90^{\circ}$
phase between basal shear $\sin kx$ and dynamic topography $\cos kx$.

5.text:
With the $\sin kx$ harmonic the steady Stokes field can be written with a
stream function

$$
\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx ,\qquad
u_{x}=F'\sin kx ,\qquad w=-kF\cos kx ,
$$

so that

$$
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}F=0 ,\qquad D\equiv d/dz , 
$$

$$
F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[F''+k^{2}F\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[F'''-3k^{2}F'\Bigr]\cos kx ,
$$

$$
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[F'''-k^{2}F'\Bigr],\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu kF'\; .
$$

In the quasi-static limit the material free surface is $w(0)=\dot e$,
$u_{x}(0)=0$ . On the steady branch

$$
F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0,
 $$

i.e. $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and, up to an inessential additive constant,

$$
F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz,\qquad c=-b/k ,
$$

so that $w_{z}(0)= -kF'(0)=0$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)\cos kx ,
\qquad F'''(0)=2bk^{2} .
$$

Hence with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)=2\mu kb ,\qquad
b=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{2\mu k} ,
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ being
absorbed in the sign.

At the base
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\frac{\mu}{k}F'''(h)-3\mu kF'(h)=0
\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h),
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\bigl[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\bigr]=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
\end{equation*}
Put $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$.  With $c=-b/k$

$$
F'(h)=dkh\,C_{h}+(b h+d)S_{h},\qquad
F'''(h)=2bk^{3}C_{h}+2dk^{3}hS_{h}+k^{3}buS_{h}+k^{3}duC_{h},
$$

$F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ is

$$
b\bigl[C_{h}-uS_{h}\bigr]=duC_{h},
\tag{3}
$$

and

$$
F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k\Bigl[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}\Bigr].
$$

Hence with (3)

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\Bigl[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}\Bigr]
      =2k b\,\frac{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{uC_{h}} .
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b
     =S_{0}\,\frac{uC_{h}}{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}},\qquad u=kh,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Bigl[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Bigr]^{-1}>0,
$$
$u=kh$, the sign being the usual $90^{\circ}$ shift between
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ and the topography $\propto\cos kx$.
In particular

$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})\quad u\ll1,\qquad
\chi(u)\sim2u\,e^{-u}\to0\quad u\gg1,
$$

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47\quad {\rm at}\quad kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2 .
$$

For the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$ mode this is the familiar
order-unity viscous-isostatic transfer

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad \chi_{0}\approx\frac12 ,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\approx \tfrac12\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow
\cos$ phase.  In the long wave lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ so that
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

With the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $F(h)=0$ the same
physics is written as 

$\chi_{0}(u)=u\big[\cosh u+u\sinh u\big]^{-1}$,
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(u)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which coincides with the
expression above to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and gives
$\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$.  The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+
\cosh^{2}u]$ form is the steady Stokes transfer for the stated
conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ with no imposed
$w(h)=0$.  This is the $O(1/2)$ dynamic-topography factor normally
quoted in the literature. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the stream-function bookkeeping is the place where the different numerators come from, and once the viscous normal stress at the free surface is handled consistently the denominator collapses to the familiar impermeable-base form.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with the Stokes sign
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= [\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.
The steady material surface is
$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$ so that
$u_{x}(0)=w(0)=0$ and $w_{,z}(0)=-k\Phi'(0)=0$.
Hence the viscous part of the normal traction vanishes identically at the top,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-p(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,
and with $\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2}$ for
$\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx$.
With the dynamic topography prescription
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$ this is

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$,    \tag{1}
and the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term is already zero at $z=0$ by $u_{x}(0)=0$.

At the base the physical condition is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.
$\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
and the imposed shear
$\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.
With $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$,

$\Phi'(h)=dkhC_{h}+(b h+d)S_{h}$,
and $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives

$b\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]=d\,uC_{h}$,   \tag{2}
the usual $p(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ link.

For a steady sheet the base is impermeable, $\Phi(h)=0$ in the chosen
normalisation, which removes the additive constant in the biharmonic
solution and makes (2) the only independent normal-stress condition at
$z=h$.  Using (2),

$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}\big]$,
so that with (2)

$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\big[C_{h}+uS_{h}\big]$.

Hence
$$
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\,\frac{1}{C_{h}+uS_{h}},
$$
and from (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b
       =\frac{S_{0}}{C_{h}+uS_{h}},
$$

i.e. in modulus with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase absorbed in the sign,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
      =\frac{kh}{\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh}>0,
$$

up to the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement.  This is
$[u/\cosh u+\cosh u/u]^{-1}$ in the usual notation.

Now
$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$,
$\chi(u)\to0$ exponentially for $u\gg1$, and
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, i.e. the familiar order-unity
dynamic topography $e_{s}\simeq\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$kh=O(1)$ with the correct lubrication limit $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$.

The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ form obtained by Colleagues 1,3,5 is
obtained if one keeps $P(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two independent
conditions together with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  Once $u_{x}(0)=0$ is
imposed $W'(0)=0$ identically, so $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-p(0)$ exactly and the
$2\mu W'$ viscous normal stress is already absorbed.  Retaining it a
second time in the elimination produces the extra $\cosh^{2}u$ term in
the denominator and the $u\cosh u$ numerator.  The same bookkeeping
gives the $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ sinh-numerator that Colleague 6
quotes, which has the wrong long-wave asymptotics
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ and can be discarded on lubrication grounds.

With the impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$ the pressure
contribution $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ is absorbed in
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and the compact transfer function
$\chi(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ is the conventional viscous-isostatic
response to $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, with the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase
between basal shear $\sin kx$ and surface topography $\cos kx$.  This
coincides with the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ expression to $O(u)$
in the long wave limit, the difference being precisely the spurious
double counting of the viscous normal stress at the free surface once
$W'(0)=0$ has been imposed. ∎

public_text.2:
With the harmonic mode

$$
\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$ \nabla^{4}\psi =0$ gives $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with
$\sigma_{ij}=-p\delta_{ij}+2\mu e_{ij}$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\Big[\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad p=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] .
$$

On the material steady free surface

$$
u_{x}(0)=0,\qquad w(0)=0\Longleftrightarrow 
\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

so that up to an additive constant

$$
\Phi(z)=b\,z\cosh kz +\big(c+dz\big)\sinh kz ,\qquad 
c=-\frac{b}{k},
$$

and $w_{,z}(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  Then

$$
\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-p(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
            =2\mu k\,b\cos kx .
$$

Hence on the steady branch, with the buoyancy renormalisation
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k\,b,\qquad 
e_{s}\propto\cos kx ,
\end{equation*}
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$
being absorbed in the sign.

At the base $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\tag{1}
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}. \tag{2}
$$

Put $u=kh$, $C_{u}=\cosh u$, $S_{u}=\sinh u$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi'(h)=Dk uC_{u}+(Bu+D)S_{u},\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)=k^{2}\!\Big[3DS_{u}+2BC_{u}+DuC_{u}+BuS_{u}\Big],
$$

where $B=b$, $D=d$.  Condition (1) is

$$
B\big[C_{u}-uS_{u}\big]=DuC_{u},
\qquad 
D=B\frac{C_{u}-uS_{u}}{uC_{u}} .
$$

Then

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\Big[C_{u}(Bu+D)+DuS_{u}\Big]
       =2kB\frac{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}{uC_{u}} .
$$

Hence from (2)

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2kB\frac{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}{uC_{u}},\qquad
B=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\frac{uC_{u}}{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}} .
$$

With $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kB$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},\qquad u=kh,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
      =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
$$

the sign being the usual $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$
phase shift.  In particular

$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1,\qquad 
\chi(u)\sim2u\,e^{-u}\to0,\;u\gg1,
$$

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47\quad{\rm at}\quad kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}\approx \tfrac12,
$$

the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography.  The long-wave
lubrication limit is $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
and the exponential screening for $kh\gg1$ is obtained.  The
$u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ form is the same response with the additional
impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$ imposed in
addition to the four conditions quoted in the statement; with the
four stated conditions $\Phi(h)=0$ is not required and the transfer
function above is the conventional $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ viscous
isostatic response, often quoted as $e_{s}\approx \tfrac12\,
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\sim1$.  Up to sign this is the $e_{s}\propto
S_{0}$ steady dynamic topography with the $90^{\circ}$ phase between
basal shear $\sin kx$ and surface topography $\cos kx$. ∎
public_text.4:
I think the bookkeeping of the viscous normal stress at the free surface is the point where the different algebraic forms diverge, and it is worth re-checking it very carefully.

With the stream function $\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, the Stokes stresses are
\[
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=\Big[\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx
          =-P+2\mu w_{,z},
\]
with $P=-(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.
The steady material free surface is
\[
w(0)=0,\qquad u_x(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0 .
\]
Hence $w_{,z}(0)=-k\Phi'(0)=0$ identically, so that on the top
\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
\]
The $2\mu w_{,z}$ viscous normal stress is already zero by $u_x(0)=0$; it should not be kept as an independent contribution after the kinematic condition is imposed. With $\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,
\[
\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx .
\]
With the buoyancy condition $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_s\cos kx$,
\[
\Delta\rho g e_s =2\mu k b, \tag{1}
\]
so the surface topography is fixed by the single constant $b$ and there is no residual $2\mu W'(0)$ term to carry through the elimination.

At the base
\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h), \tag{2}
\]
i.e. $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$, and the imposed shear
\[
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_0 . \tag{3}
\]
Writing $u=kh$, $c_h=\cosh u$, $s_h=\sinh u$,
\[
\Phi'(h)=dkh\,c_h+(bkh+d)s_h .
\]
Eq.(2) is
\[
b\big[c_h-u s_h\big]=d\,u c_h , \tag{4}
\]
and
\[
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)c_h+ud s_h\big].
\]
Eliminating $d$ with (4) in (3) gives
\[
\frac{S_0}{\mu}=2k b\big[c_h+u s_h\big],
\]
so that
\[
b=\frac{S_0}{2k\mu}\frac{1}{c_h+u s_h}.
\]
With (1)
\[
\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k b=\frac{S_0\,u}{c_h+u s_h},
\]
up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase. In modulus
\[
e_s=\chi(u)\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u},\qquad u=kh,
\]
i.e. $\chi(u)=\big[u/\cosh u+\cosh u/u\big]^{-1}$ on the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$ which removes the additive constant in the biharmonic solution.

This gives the expected asymptotics
\[
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1,\qquad 
\chi(u)\to0,\;u\gg1,
\]
with $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, the familiar $O(1/2)$ viscous-isostatic value for $kh=O(1)$ and the linear lubrication limit $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ form that appears in 1,3,5 is obtained if the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term is kept symbolically in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu w_{,z}(0)$ after $w_{,z}(0)=0$ has already been imposed by $u_x(0)=0$, and then $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ is used together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two independent conditions. Once $W'(0)=0$ is enforced, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly and the extra $2\mu W'$ is already absorbed; retaining it a second time in the elimination produces the additional $\cosh^{2}u$ term in the denominator. The two expressions coincide only to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi\sim kh$, which is why the long-wave lubrication limit is the same in both camps.

The $u\sinh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ sinh-numerator form gives $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$, a quadratic long-wave limit inconsistent with the lubrication expectation for a finite thickness viscous sheet, and can be discarded on asymptotic grounds.

With the usual $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy renormalisation this is the compact steady transfer function most commonly quoted for a viscous sheet with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$ and the $90^{\circ}$ phase between basal shear $\sin kx$ and surface topography $\cos kx$.
public_text.1:
With the $\sin kx$ mode put
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$, $D=d/dz$,

$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big]$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\big[-P-2\mu kF'\big]\cos kx
          =\mu k^{-1}\big[F'''-3k^{2}F'\big]\cos kx$.

In the steady material limit $w(0)=u_{x}(0)=0$,

$F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0$,

so that with an inessential constant removed

$F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $b=-kc$,

$F'(0)=0$, $w_{z}(0)=0$.
Then

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$, 
$F'''(0)=2k^{2}b$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
\qquad b=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{2\mu k}\;,
\tag{1}
$$
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being absorbed in the sign.

At $z=h$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,

i.e. with $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$,

$C_{h}\big[b-ku d\big]=2S_{h}\big[d+ku b\big]$,
$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\Big[C_{h}\big(d+k b h\big)+k d hS_{h}\Big]$ .

With $b=-kc$ the normal-traction condition gives
$d=c\,u^{-1}\big[u\tanh u-1\big]$ and after elimination of $d$

$$
\mu\,2k\Big\{d\big[C_{h}+uS_{h}\big]-k^{2}c\,h C_{h}\Big\}=S_{0},
$$

i.e.

$$
c=-\frac{S_{0}h^{2}C_{h}}{2\mu u\big[u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\big]},\qquad
b=-kc=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\frac{uC_{h}}{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}} .
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b
   =S_{0}\,\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},\qquad u=kh,
$$

so that in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad u=kh,
$$

$e_{s}\propto\cos kx$ against $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, the usual
$90^{\circ}$ phase shift.  In particular

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\to0$,  $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0,\;u\to\infty$,

$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45-0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0-1.2$,

and for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}\approx\frac12 ,
$$

i.e. the familiar viscous-isostatic
$e_{s}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$ dynamic topography, the $-$ sign
being the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase.  In the long wave
lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ so that $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

With the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$,
$W(h)=0$, the same stream function is usually written in the compact
form $\chi_{0}(u)=u\big[\cosh u+u\sinh u\big]^{-1}$, which coincides
with the expression above to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and gives
$\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$.  The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$
numerator is obtained by double counting the $2\mu w_{z}$ viscous normal
stress after $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ has already been used and gives the
wrong quadratic long-wave limit $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$.  The $u\cosh u/
[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ screening is the steady Stokes response to
$\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under the stated conditions
$F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, and reduces to the quoted
$\chi\approx1/2$ for $kh\sim O(1)$. ∎
public_text.6:
I think we are now close on the common denominator $u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u$ and the only remaining physical point is the way the normal traction is closed at the two boundaries.

Put $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with the usual Stokes sign
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= [\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.  
The steady material free surface is
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ so that $w_{,z}(0)=0$ identically.
Hence
\[
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx,
\qquad\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2},
\]
and with the normalisation $\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,
\[
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b,
\tag{1}
\]
the $2\mu w_{,z}$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ being identically zero at $z=0$
once $u_{x}(0)=0$ is imposed. There is therefore no independent
$2\mu W'(0)$ contribution to keep at the top; $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$
exactly.

At the base the problem states $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, not $P(h)=0$.  With
$w_{,z}=-k\Phi'$,
\[
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff -P(h)+2\mu w_{,z}(h)=0\iff
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),
\tag{2}
\]
i.e. $U''-3k^{2}U=0$ for $U=\Phi'$.  This is the physical coupling of
pressure and viscous normal stress at the asthenosphere interface.
With $u=kh$, $c_{h}=\cosh u$, $s_{h}=\sinh u$,
\[
\Phi'(h)=dkh c_{h}+(bh+d)s_{h},\qquad
b[c_{h}-u s_{h}]=d\,u c_{h},
\tag{3}
\]
which is (2). The imposed basal shear is
\[
\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0},
\tag{4}
\]
and
\[
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)c_{h}+ud\,s_{h}\big].
\]
Eliminating $d$ with (3) in (4) gives
\[
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\,
\frac{u\,s_{h}\big[c_{h}^{2}+u^{2}\big]+u^{2}c_{h}s_{h}}{c_{h}^{2}+u^{2}}
=2k b\,\frac{u s_{h}}{c_{h}^{2}+u^{2}}\,
\Big[c_{h}^{2}+u^{2}+u\,c_{h}s_{h}\Big],
\]
and using (3) to replace the bracket one obtains the closed form
\[
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\,
\frac{u\,s_{h}}{u^{2}+c_{h}^{2}} .
\]
With (1)
\[
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b
   =S_{0}\,\frac{u\sinh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},
\qquad u=kh,
\]
up to the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$,
i.e. in modulus
\[
e_{s}= \chi(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u\,\sinh u}{\cosh^{2}u+u^{2}} .
\]
This is the transfer function that follows from the full
$\sigma_{zz}=-P+2\mu w_{,z}$ at both boundaries with the free-surface
kinematic conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and the physical base condition
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$.  In particular
\[
\chi(u)=\frac{u^{2}}{2}+O(u^{4}),\;u\ll1,\qquad
\chi(u)\sim u e^{-u},\;u\gg1,
\]
so the exponential screening for $kh\gg1$ is recovered and the long-wave
lubrication screening is quadratic, as it must be when the viscous normal
stress $2\mu w_{,z}$ is retained at the base through (2).

The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ form of Colleagues 1,3,5 is obtained if
the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term is dropped at the base, i.e. if $P(h)=0$ is used
instead of $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, or equivalently if the $2\mu W'$ contribution
is kept a second time after $W'(0)=0$ has already been imposed by
$u_{x}(0)=0$.  That is the double counting that Colleague 4 has been
pointing out: once $W'(0)=0$ the free-surface normal traction is
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly, and re-introducing an effective
$2\mu W'$ in the elimination produces the extra $\cosh$ factor in the
numerator.

The compact form $\chi_{0}=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ that Colleague 4 now
writes down is the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ result after the
additional impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$ is imposed.  The two
expressions coincide only to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$, which is why Colleague 2’s
claim of algebraic equivalence between
$u\cosh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ and $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ cannot hold
exactly.  The minimal, physically consistent set
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives the
$\sinh$-numerator transfer function above, with the familiar
$O(1/2)$ geophysical value for $kh\sim O(1)$ and the required $90^{\circ}$
phase between basal shear $\sin kx$ and dynamic topography $\cos kx$.
public_text.5:
With the $\sin kx$ harmonic the steady Stokes field can be written with a
stream function

$$
\psi(x,z)=F(z)\sin kx ,\qquad
u_{x}=F'\sin kx ,\qquad w=-kF\cos kx ,
$$

so that

$$
\bigl(D^{2}-k^{2}\bigr)^{2}F=0 ,\qquad D\equiv d/dz , 
$$

$$
F(z)=(a+bz)\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\bigl[F''+k^{2}F\bigr]\sin kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[F'''-3k^{2}F'\Bigr]\cos kx ,
$$

$$
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Bigl[F'''-k^{2}F'\Bigr],\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu kF'\; .
$$

In the quasi-static limit the material free surface is $w(0)=\dot e$,
$u_{x}(0)=0$ . On the steady branch

$$
F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0,
 $$

i.e. $a=0$, $b+kc=0$ and, up to an inessential additive constant,

$$
F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz,\qquad c=-b/k ,
$$

so that $w_{z}(0)= -kF'(0)=0$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)\cos kx ,
\qquad F'''(0)=2bk^{2} .
$$

Hence with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)=2\mu kb ,\qquad
b=\frac{\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}}{2\mu k} ,
\tag{1}
\end{equation*}
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ being
absorbed in the sign.

At the base
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\frac{\mu}{k}F'''(h)-3\mu kF'(h)=0
\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h),
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation*}
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\bigl[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\bigr]=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
\end{equation*}
Put $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$.  With $c=-b/k$

$$
F'(h)=dkh\,C_{h}+(b h+d)S_{h},\qquad
F'''(h)=2bk^{3}C_{h}+2dk^{3}hS_{h}+k^{3}buS_{h}+k^{3}duC_{h},
$$

$F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ is

$$
b\bigl[C_{h}-uS_{h}\bigr]=duC_{h},
\tag{3}
$$

and

$$
F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k\Bigl[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}\Bigr].
$$

Hence with (3)

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k\Bigl[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}\Bigr]
      =2k b\,\frac{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{uC_{h}} .
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b
     =S_{0}\,\frac{uC_{h}}{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}},\qquad u=kh,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(kh)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Bigl[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Bigr]^{-1}>0,
$$
$u=kh$, the sign being the usual $90^{\circ}$ shift between
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ and the topography $\propto\cos kx$.
In particular

$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})\quad u\ll1,\qquad
\chi(u)\sim2u\,e^{-u}\to0\quad u\gg1,
$$

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47\quad {\rm at}\quad kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2 .
$$

For the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$ mode this is the familiar
order-unity viscous-isostatic transfer

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad \chi_{0}\approx\frac12 ,
$$

i.e. $e_{s}\approx \tfrac12\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ up to the $\sin\leftrightarrow
\cos$ phase.  In the long wave lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ so that
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

With the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $F(h)=0$ the same
physics is written as 

$\chi_{0}(u)=u\big[\cosh u+u\sinh u\big]^{-1}$,
$e_{s}= \chi_{0}(u)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, which coincides with the
expression above to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and gives
$\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$.  The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+
\cosh^{2}u]$ form is the steady Stokes transfer for the stated
conditions $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ with no imposed
$w(h)=0$.  This is the $O(1/2)$ dynamic-topography factor normally
quoted in the literature. ∎
public_text.7:
I think the stream-function bookkeeping is the place where the different numerators come from, and once the viscous normal stress at the free surface is handled consistently the denominator collapses to the familiar impermeable-base form.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$,
$u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$ and with the Stokes sign
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= [\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.
The steady material surface is
$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$ so that
$u_{x}(0)=w(0)=0$ and $w_{,z}(0)=-k\Phi'(0)=0$.
Hence the viscous part of the normal traction vanishes identically at the top,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-p(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,
and with $\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2}$ for
$\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx$.
With the dynamic topography prescription
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$ this is

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$,    \tag{1}
and the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term is already zero at $z=0$ by $u_{x}(0)=0$.

At the base the physical condition is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.
$\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$,
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
and the imposed shear
$\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.
With $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$,

$\Phi'(h)=dkhC_{h}+(b h+d)S_{h}$,
and $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives

$b\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]=d\,uC_{h}$,   \tag{2}
the usual $p(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ link.

For a steady sheet the base is impermeable, $\Phi(h)=0$ in the chosen
normalisation, which removes the additive constant in the biharmonic
solution and makes (2) the only independent normal-stress condition at
$z=h$.  Using (2),

$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}\big]$,
so that with (2)

$\displaystyle\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\big[C_{h}+uS_{h}\big]$.

Hence
$$
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\,\frac{1}{C_{h}+uS_{h}},
$$
and from (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b
       =\frac{S_{0}}{C_{h}+uS_{h}},
$$

i.e. in modulus with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase absorbed in the sign,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
      =\frac{kh}{\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh}>0,
$$

up to the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement.  This is
$[u/\cosh u+\cosh u/u]^{-1}$ in the usual notation.

Now
$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$,
$\chi(u)\to0$ exponentially for $u\gg1$, and
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, i.e. the familiar order-unity
dynamic topography $e_{s}\simeq\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for
$kh=O(1)$ with the correct lubrication limit $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$.

The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ form obtained by Colleagues 1,3,5 is
obtained if one keeps $P(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two independent
conditions together with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  Once $u_{x}(0)=0$ is
imposed $W'(0)=0$ identically, so $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-p(0)$ exactly and the
$2\mu W'$ viscous normal stress is already absorbed.  Retaining it a
second time in the elimination produces the extra $\cosh^{2}u$ term in
the denominator and the $u\cosh u$ numerator.  The same bookkeeping
gives the $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ sinh-numerator that Colleague 6
quotes, which has the wrong long-wave asymptotics
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ and can be discarded on lubrication grounds.

With the impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$ the pressure
contribution $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ is absorbed in
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and the compact transfer function
$\chi(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ is the conventional viscous-isostatic
response to $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$, with the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase
between basal shear $\sin kx$ and surface topography $\cos kx$.  This
coincides with the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ expression to $O(u)$
in the long wave limit, the difference being precisely the spurious
double counting of the viscous normal stress at the free surface once
$W'(0)=0$ has been imposed. ∎

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$ and

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$, $p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.

Steady material free surface: $u_x(0)=0$, $w(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$.
Hence $\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$, $w_{,z}(0)=0$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\mu k^{-1}2bk^{2}=2\mu k b$
so with the stated normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_s\cos kx$,
$\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k b$, $e_s\propto\cos kx$ vs $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$.
With $u=kh$, $C_u=\cosh u$, $S_u=\sinh u$,

$\Phi'(h)=DuC_u+(Bu+D)S_u$, $\Phi'''(h)=k^2[3DS_u+2BC_u+DuC_u+BuS_u]$,
$B=b$, $D=d$,
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)\iff B(C_u-uS_u)=DuC_u$,
$D=B(C_u-uS_u)/uC_u$,

$\Phi''+k^2\Phi\big|_h =2k[C_u(Bu+D)+DuS_u]=2kB\frac{u^2+C_u^2}{uC_u}$.

Hence
$S_0/\mu=2kB\frac{u^2+C_u^2}{uC_u}$,
$B=\frac{S_0}{2\mu k}\frac{uC_u}{u^2+C_u^2}$,
$\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k B=S_0\frac{uC_u}{u^2+C_u^2}$.

In modulus
$e_s=\chi(u)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^2+\cosh^2u}=[u/\cosh u+\cosh u/u]^{-1}>0$,
$u=kh$.

Asymptotics: $\chi=u+O(u^3)$, $u\ll1$, $\chi\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$, $u\gg1$;
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$, i.e. $e_s\approx\chi_0S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_0\approx1/2$ for $kh=O(1)$. Long-wave lubrication $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

Current round consensus: Colleagues 1,2,3,5 obtain the same $u\cosh u/(u^2+\cosh^2u)$ transfer with the four stated conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$. Colleagues 4,7 obtain $\chi_0(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ which is the same physics under the extra impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$ imposed in addition to $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. With the problem as stated $\Phi(h)=0$ is not required.
Colleague 6’s $u\sinh u/(u^2+\cosh^2u)$ gives $\chi\sim u^2/2$ for $u\ll1$, inconsistent with the lubrication expectation $\chi\sim u$. The double counting of the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term after $W'(0)=0$ has been identified as the source of the $u/[\cosh+u\sinh]$ vs $u\cosh/(u^2+\cosh^2)$ difference. Phase is the usual $90^\circ$, $e_s\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$, absorbed in sign. The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the usual buoyancy renormalisation. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic sin kx mode can be written with a stream function
ψ=F(z) sin kx, u_x=F' sin kx, w=-kF cos kx, (D²-k²)²F=0,
F(z)=(a+bz)cosh kz+(c+dz)sinh kz, D=d/dz, u=kh.
The steady material free surface is taken as u_x(0)=0, w(0)=0 i.e.
F(0)=0, F'(0)=0, so a=0, b+kc=0 and up to an inessential constant
F=bz cosh kz+(c+dz)sinh kz, c=-b/k. With the Stokes sign
σ_xz=μ[F''+k²F] sin kx,
P=-(μ/k)[F'''-k²F'], σ_zz=[-P-2μkF'] cos kx=(μ/k)[F'''-3k²F'] cos kx.
Then σ_zz(0)=(μ/k)F'''(0)cos kx, F'''(0)=2k²b, so on the steady branch
Δρ g e_s =2μ k b, the 90° phase e_s∝cos kx, τ_b∝sin kx being absorbed in sign.

The stated base conditions are σ_zz(h)=0 and σ_xz(h)=S0,
σ_zz(h)=0⇔F'''(h)=3k²F'(h), μ[F''(h)+k²F(h)]=S0,
with no imposed Φ(h)=0, w(h)=0. With u=kh, C_h=cosh u, S_h=sinh u,
F'''(h)=3k²F'(h) gives b[C_h-uS_h]=duC_h, d=b(C_h-uS_h)/(uC_h), and
S0/μ=2k[(d+bu)C_h+udS_h]. Hence
b= S0/(2μk) · u C_h/(u²+C_h²) , d=b/u[1-u tanh u],
and
Δρ g e_s=2μk b= S0·u C_h/(u²+C_h²).
In modulus
e_s=χ(u) S0/Δρ g, χ(u)=u cosh u/[u²+cosh²u]=[u/cosh u+cosh u/u]⁻¹>0,
u=kh.
Limits χ=u+O(u³), u≪1; χ∼2u e^{-u}→0, u≫1;

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady 2-D Stokes response with $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$ is $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$. With the usual sign
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[F'''-3k^{2}F']\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$.
Top steady material conditions are $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$, i.e. $u_{x}(0)=w(0)=0$ and $w_{z}(0)=0$ identically, so that
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$. With $F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $b+kc=0$,
$F'''(0)=2bk^{2}$ and $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$ the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in the sign.
Base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)]=S_{0}$.
With $u=kh$, $c_{h}=\cosh u$, $s_{h}=\sinh u$, $c=-b/k$ the normal-traction condition gives
$b\big[c_{h}-u s_{h}\big]=du c_{h}$ and after elimination
$F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k b\,[u^{2}+c_{h}^{2}]/[u c_{h}]$.
Hence
$b=\dfrac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\dfrac{u c_{h}}{u^{2}+c_{h}^{2}}$, $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$, i.e. in modulus
$e_{s}= \chi(u) S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(u)=\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
      =\Big[\dfrac{u}{\cosh u}+\dfrac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0$, $u=kh$.
Asymptotics: $\chi=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$ for $u\gg1$, $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$, and the geophysical $kh=O(1)$ estimate $e_{s}\simeq\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The long-wave lubrication limit is $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ form $\chi_{B}=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ is the same physics with the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $F(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$ imposed in addition to the four stated conditions; it coincides with $\chi$ to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and gives $\chi_{B}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$.
The sinh-numerator form $\chi_{C}=u\sinh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ gives $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$ and is ruled out by the lubrication expectation.
The disagreement in round 3 is the bookkeeping of the $2\mu w_{z}$ viscous normal stress after $w_{z}(0)=0$ is already imposed by $u_{x}(0)=0$: once $F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly. Retaining $2\mu w_{z}$ a second time in the elimination produces the extra $\cosh^{2}u$ term and the $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ vs $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ discrepancy. With the stated conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the consistent transfer function is the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ screening, with the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase between basal shear $\sin kx$ and topography $\cos kx$, up to the conventional $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ renormalisation.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $D=d/dz$.
With the material steady free surface $w(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ on the
steady branch

$F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0$,

so that up to an additive constant

$F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $b+ck=0$, $c=-b/k$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[F'''-3k^{2}F']\cos kx=-P-2\mu kF'\cos kx$.

Hence $w_{,z}(0)=-kF'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$, $F'''(0)=k^{2}(3b+ck)=2bk^{2}$,
so that with the buoyancy renormalisation $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=2\mu k b$, 
$e_{s}\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, the usual $90^{\circ}$
phase being absorbed in the sign.

At the base the stated conditions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)]=S_{0}$.
With $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$ and $b=-kc$,

$F'(h)=S_{h}(bu+d)+duC_{h}$,
$F'''(h)=k^{2}[2bC_{h}+buS_{h}+3dS_{h}+duC_{h}]$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$b[C_{h}-uS_{h}]=duC_{h}$, $d=b(C_{h}-uS_{h})/uC_{h}$.

Then
$F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k\Big[(bu+d)C_{h}+duS_{h}\Big]
      =2kb\,\dfrac{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{uC_{h}}$,
so that

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\,\dfrac{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{uC_{h}}$,

$b=\dfrac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\dfrac{uC_{h}}{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}$.

With $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}$,
$u=kh$,

i.e. in modulus

$e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx$,
$\displaystyle 
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0$.

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}$ for $u\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$ and
$\chi\approx\frac12$ for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$ mode,
the familiar $e_{s}\simeq \tfrac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous-isostatic
dynamic topography with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase. In the long-wave lubrication limit $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ form quoted by Colleagues 4 and 7 is the
same physics with the additional impermeable-base normalisation
$F(h)=0\iff W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, which is not imposed in the
statement. With $F(h)=0$ one obtains the compact transfer
$\chi_{0}(u)=u[\cosh u+u\sinh u]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, coinciding with the
expression above to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$. 
Colleague 6’s $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ numerator gives
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$, inconsistent with the lubrication
$e_{s}\sim kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ limit, and is the result of double
counting the $2\mu w_{z}$ viscous normal stress after $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
has been used.

Hence with the four stated conditions $F(0)=F'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$,
the admissible steady response is
$\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$, $\chi\approx1/2$ for $kh\sim O(1)$,
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$ versus $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being the conventional dynamic-topography sign. ∎

reflection_text.2:
The stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives $(D^2-k^2)^2\Phi=0$ and

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$, $p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.

Steady material free surface: $u_x(0)=0$, $w(0)=0\iff\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$.
Hence $\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$, $w_{,z}(0)=0$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\mu k^{-1}2bk^{2}=2\mu k b$
so with the stated normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_s\cos kx$,
$\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k b$, $e_s\propto\cos kx$ vs $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$.

Base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$.
With $u=kh$, $C_u=\cosh u$, $S_u=\sinh u$,

$\Phi'(h)=DuC_u+(Bu+D)S_u$, $\Phi'''(h)=k^2[3DS_u+2BC_u+DuC_u+BuS_u]$,
$B=b$, $D=d$,
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)\iff B(C_u-uS_u)=DuC_u$,
$D=B(C_u-uS_u)/uC_u$,

$\Phi''+k^2\Phi\big|_h =2k[C_u(Bu+D)+DuS_u]=2kB\frac{u^2+C_u^2}{uC_u}$.

Hence
$S_0/\mu=2kB\frac{u^2+C_u^2}{uC_u}$,
$B=\frac{S_0}{2\mu k}\frac{uC_u}{u^2+C_u^2}$,
$\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k B=S_0\frac{uC_u}{u^2+C_u^2}$.

In modulus
$e_s=\chi(u)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^2+\cosh^2u}=[u/\cosh u+\cosh u/u]^{-1}>0$,
$u=kh$.

Asymptotics: $\chi=u+O(u^3)$, $u\ll1$, $\chi\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$, $u\gg1$;
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$, i.e. $e_s\approx\chi_0S_0/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_0\approx1/2$ for $kh=O(1)$. Long-wave lubrication $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

Current round consensus: Colleagues 1,2,3,5 obtain the same $u\cosh u/(u^2+\cosh^2u)$ transfer with the four stated conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$. Colleagues 4,7 obtain $\chi_0(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ which is the same physics under the extra impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$ imposed in addition to $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. With the problem as stated $\Phi(h)=0$ is not required.
Colleague 6’s $u\sinh u/(u^2+\cosh^2u)$ gives $\chi\sim u^2/2$ for $u\ll1$, inconsistent with the lubrication expectation $\chi\sim u$. The double counting of the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term after $W'(0)=0$ has been identified as the source of the $u/[\cosh+u\sinh]$ vs $u\cosh/(u^2+\cosh^2)$ difference. Phase is the usual $90^\circ$, $e_s\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_b\propto\sin kx$, absorbed in sign. The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the usual buoyancy renormalisation. ∎

P=-(μ/k)[F'''-k²F'], σ_zz=[-P-2μkF'] cos kx=(μ/k)[F'''-3k²F'] cos kx.

Δρ g e_s =2μ k b, the 90° phase e_s∝cos kx, τ_b∝sin kx being absorbed in sign.

The stated base conditions are σ_zz(h)=0 and σ_xz(h)=S0,
σ_zz(h)=0⇔F'''(h)=3k²F'(h), μ[F''(h)+k²F(h)]=S0,
with no imposed Φ(h)=0, w(h)=0. With u=kh, C_h=cosh u, S_h=sinh u,
F'''(h)=3k²F'(h) gives b[C_h-uS_h]=duC_h, d=b(C_h-uS_h)/(uC_h), and
S0/μ=2k[(d+bu)C_h+udS_h]. Hence
b= S0/(2μk) · u C_h/(u²+C_h²) , d=b/u[1-u tanh u],
and
Δρ g e_s=2μk b= S0·u C_h/(u²+C_h²).
In modulus
e_s=χ(u) S0/Δρ g, χ(u)=u cosh u/[u²+cosh²u]=[u/cosh u+cosh u/u]⁻¹>0,
u=kh.
Limits χ=u+O(u³), u≪1; χ∼2u e^{-u}→0, u≫1;
χ_max≈0.45–0.47 at kh≈1.0–1.2, and for the geologically relevant kh=O(1)
χ0≈½, e_s≈½ S0/Δρ g, the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography
with the sin kx→cos kx 90° phase.

Round 3 consensus:
Colleagues 1,2,3,5 obtain the same u cosh u/[u²+cosh²u] transfer with
F(0)=F'(0)=0, σ_zz(h)=0, σ_xz(h)=S0 and Δρ g e_s=2μk b.
Colleagues 4,7 obtain the compact impermeable-base normalisation
Φ(h)=0, W(h)=0, i.e. an extra condition F(h)=0, which removes the additive
constant in the biharmonic solution and gives
χ0(u)=u/[cosh u+u sinh u]=u cosh u/[u²+cosh²u] to O(u) for u≪1,
χ0_max≈0.39 at kh≈0.8, χ0≈u for u≪1. This is the form most often quoted
in the literature for a viscous sheet with an impermeable base.
The two forms coincide to O(u) in the lubrication limit; the difference
is precisely the extra Φ(h)=0 / W(h)=0 condition not stated in the problem.

Colleague 6’s sinh-numerator χ_s=u sinh u/[u²+cosh²u] gives
χ_s≈u²/2 for u≪1, i.e. a quadratic long-wave limit, inconsistent with the
lubrication expectation χ∼u for a finite-thickness viscous sheet with the
stated σ_zz(h)=0, u_x(0)=0 conditions, and is rejected on asymptotic grounds.
The double-counting issue noted by Colleague 4 is that w_z(0)=-kF'(0)=0
by u_x(0)=0, so σ_zz(0)=-P(0) exactly; retaining a symbolic 2μw_z term
after imposing F'(0)=0 produces the extra cosh² term in the denominator
and the alternative numerators. Once W'(0)=0 is enforced, the
σ_zz=-P+2μw_z bookkeeping is consistent and the u cosh u/[u²+cosh²u]
response is the correct steady Stokes transfer for the four conditions
F(0)=F'(0)=0, σ_zz(0)=Δρ g e, σ_zz(h)=0, σ_xz(h)=S0 with no imposed
w(h)=0. With the conventional Δρ renormalisation this is the O(½)
dynamic-topography factor normally quoted as e_s≈χ S0/Δρ g,
χ≈½ for kh∼O(1). If the conventional impermeable-base normalisation
Φ(h)=0 is adopted the quoted compact form is χ0=u/[cosh u+u sinh u],
numerically ≈½ for kh∼1. Unresolved is whether the physical base should be
taken impermeable; the problem statement as written does not impose
w(h)=0, so the u cosh u/[u²+cosh²u] form is the literal solution.

reflection_text.3:
The steady 2-D Stokes response with $\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$ is $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$. With the usual sign
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[F'''-3k^{2}F']\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$.
Top steady material conditions are $F(0)=0$, $F'(0)=0$, i.e. $u_{x}(0)=w(0)=0$ and $w_{z}(0)=0$ identically, so that
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$. With $F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $b+kc=0$,
$F'''(0)=2bk^{2}$ and $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$ the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in the sign.
Base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)]=S_{0}$.
With $u=kh$, $c_{h}=\cosh u$, $s_{h}=\sinh u$, $c=-b/k$ the normal-traction condition gives
$b\big[c_{h}-u s_{h}\big]=du c_{h}$ and after elimination
$F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k b\,[u^{2}+c_{h}^{2}]/[u c_{h}]$.
Hence
$b=\dfrac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\dfrac{u c_{h}}{u^{2}+c_{h}^{2}}$, $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$, i.e. in modulus
$e_{s}= \chi(u) S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(u)=\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
      =\Big[\dfrac{u}{\cosh u}+\dfrac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0$, $u=kh$.
Asymptotics: $\chi=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$ for $u\gg1$, $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$, and the geophysical $kh=O(1)$ estimate $e_{s}\simeq\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The long-wave lubrication limit is $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ form $\chi_{B}=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ is the same physics with the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $F(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$ imposed in addition to the four stated conditions; it coincides with $\chi$ to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and gives $\chi_{B}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$.
The sinh-numerator form $\chi_{C}=u\sinh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ gives $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$ and is ruled out by the lubrication expectation.
The disagreement in round 3 is the bookkeeping of the $2\mu w_{z}$ viscous normal stress after $w_{z}(0)=0$ is already imposed by $u_{x}(0)=0$: once $F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly. Retaining $2\mu w_{z}$ a second time in the elimination produces the extra $\cosh^{2}u$ term and the $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ vs $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ discrepancy. With the stated conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ the consistent transfer function is the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ screening, with the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase between basal shear $\sin kx$ and topography $\cos kx$, up to the conventional $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ renormalisation.
reflection_text.1:
The harmonic Stokes mode can be written with a stream function
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $D=d/dz$.
With the material steady free surface $w(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ on the
steady branch

$F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0$,

so that up to an additive constant

$F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $b+ck=0$, $c=-b/k$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[F'''-3k^{2}F']\cos kx=-P-2\mu kF'\cos kx$.

Hence $w_{,z}(0)=-kF'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$, $F'''(0)=k^{2}(3b+ck)=2bk^{2}$,
so that with the buoyancy renormalisation $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=2\mu k b$, 
$e_{s}\propto\cos kx$, $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, the usual $90^{\circ}$
phase being absorbed in the sign.

At the base the stated conditions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)]=S_{0}$.
With $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$ and $b=-kc$,

$F'(h)=S_{h}(bu+d)+duC_{h}$,
$F'''(h)=k^{2}[2bC_{h}+buS_{h}+3dS_{h}+duC_{h}]$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$b[C_{h}-uS_{h}]=duC_{h}$, $d=b(C_{h}-uS_{h})/uC_{h}$.

Then
$F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k\Big[(bu+d)C_{h}+duS_{h}\Big]
      =2kb\,\dfrac{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{uC_{h}}$,
so that

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\,\dfrac{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{uC_{h}}$,

$b=\dfrac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\dfrac{uC_{h}}{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}$.

With $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}$,
$u=kh$,

i.e. in modulus

$e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx$,
$\displaystyle 
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0$.

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}$ for $u\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$ and
$\chi\approx\frac12$ for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$ mode,
the familiar $e_{s}\simeq \tfrac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous-isostatic
dynamic topography with the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$
phase. In the long-wave lubrication limit $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ form quoted by Colleagues 4 and 7 is the
same physics with the additional impermeable-base normalisation
$F(h)=0\iff W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, which is not imposed in the
statement. With $F(h)=0$ one obtains the compact transfer
$\chi_{0}(u)=u[\cosh u+u\sinh u]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, coinciding with the
expression above to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$. 
Colleague 6’s $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ numerator gives
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$, inconsistent with the lubrication
$e_{s}\sim kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ limit, and is the result of double
counting the $2\mu w_{z}$ viscous normal stress after $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$
has been used.

Hence with the four stated conditions $F(0)=F'(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$,
the admissible steady response is
$\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$, $\chi\approx1/2$ for $kh\sim O(1)$,
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$ versus $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$
being the conventional dynamic-topography sign. ∎

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the point where the algebra splits is the handling of the viscous normal stress at the free surface and the way the base normal condition is used.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \Big[\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx
          =-P+2\mu w_{,z},
$$
$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad w_{,z}=-k\Phi'.
$$

On the material steady surface

$$
w(0)=0,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

Hence $w_{,z}(0)=0$ identically and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

The $2\mu w_{,z}$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ is already zero by $u_{x}(0)=0$; it should not be kept as an independent contribution after the kinematic condition is imposed. With the usual
$\Phi(z)=b z\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,

$$
\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx,
$$

so that with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b ,\tag{1}
$$
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in the sign.

At the base the physical condition quoted is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\tag{2}
$$
and the imposed shear

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}. \tag{3}
$$

With $u=kh$, $C_{u}=\cosh u$, $S_{u}=\sinh u$,

$$
\Phi'(h)=d\,uC_{u}+(b u+d)S_{u},
$$

and (2) gives

$$
b\big[C_{u}-uS_{u}\big]=d\,uC_{u}. \tag{4}
$$

In the conventional biharmonic normalisation the base is impermeable,
$\Phi(h)=0$, so the additive constant in the $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$
solution is removed and (2) is the only independent normal-stress
condition at $z=h$, i.e. $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ is absorbed in (2).

Now

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)C_{u}+u d S_{u}\big].
$$

Eliminating $d$ with (4) in (3),

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\big[C_{u}+uS_{u}\big],
$$

so that

$$
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\frac{1}{C_{u}+uS_{u}}.
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b=\frac{S_{0}}{C_{u}+uS_{u}}\,
\frac{u}{u} ,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u},\qquad u=kh,
$$

the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase between $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ and
$e_{s}\propto\cos kx$. With the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy
renormalisation this is the compact steady transfer function.

The asymptotics are the physically expected ones:

$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1,\qquad
\chi(u)\to0\;{\rm exponentially},\;u\gg1,
$$

$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, and for $kh=O(1)$
$e_{s}\simeq\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar order-unity
viscous-isostatic dynamic topography with linear lubrication limit
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Retaining the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term symbolically in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu
w_{,z}(0)$ after $w_{,z}(0)=0$ has already been imposed by $u_{x}(0)=0$, and
then using $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two
independent conditions, produces the extra $\cosh^{2}u$ in the denominator
and the $u\cosh u$ numerator. Once $W'(0)=0$ is enforced,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly and the $2\mu W'$ contribution is already
absorbed; keeping it a second time in the elimination is the double
counting noted by 4 and 7. The two forms coincide to $O(u)$ in the long
wave limit, which is why the lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ is common to
both camps, but the impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e.
$W(h)=0$, gives the clean denominator $\cosh u+u\sinh u$ and the
conventional $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ screening.

The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ sinh-numerator that appeared in an
earlier round has the wrong long-wave $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ and is
inconsistent with the lubrication expectation. With the bookkeeping above
the steady response is the compact form $\chi=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$,
with the $90^{\circ}$ phase and the familiar $O(1/2)$ value for $kh\sim1$.

\qquad u=kh,
