$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1$, $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0,\;u\gg1$,

$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$,

so that for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,   $\chi_{0}\approx\frac12$,

the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography
$e_{s}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$ with the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$
phase.  In the long wave lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$,
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The compact form $\chi_{0}(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ quoted by
Colleagues 4 and 7 is the same physics with the conventional
impermeable-base normalisation $F(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$, imposed in
addition to the four conditions stated in the problem.  With the
stated conditions $F(h)=0$ is not required and the transfer function
above is the steady Stokes response to $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$ under
$F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.  The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$
numerator gives the wrong quadratic long wave limit $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$
and is ruled out on lubrication grounds. ∎

5.text:
The steady harmonic Stokes field can be written with

$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $D=d/dz$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu [F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, 
$P=-(\mu/k)[F'''-k^{2}F']$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu kF'=
(\mu/k)[F'''-3k^{2}F']\cos kx$.

On the material free surface in the quasi–static limit

$u_{x}(0)=0,\;w(0)=0\iff F(0)=0,\;F'(0)=0$,

and with an inessential additive constant

$F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,

so that $w_{z}(0)=-kF'(0)=0$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)\cos kx$.
Now $F'''(0)=2k^{2}b$ and with the buoyancy
normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)=2\mu k b,\qquad
b=\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k},
\end{equation*}
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $ \tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$
being absorbed in the sign.

At $z=h$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ ,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff \mu[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)]=S_{0}$ .

Put $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$.  With $c=-b/k$,

$F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ gives

$b\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]=duC_{h}$, 
$d=b\,\dfrac{C_{h}-uS_{h}}{uC_{h}}$,

and

$F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}\big]$.

Eliminating $d$,
$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\,\frac{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{uC_{h}},
\qquad
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\frac{uC_{h}}{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}} .
$$

Hence on the steady branch

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b
 =S_{0}\,\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},
\qquad u=kh,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
 =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0 ,
$$

the sign being the usual $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$  $90^{\circ}$
phase shift.  In particular

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1$, 
$\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0,\;u\gg1$,

$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45$–$0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0$–$1.2$.  For the
geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}\approx\frac12,
$$

the familiar $e_{s}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$ viscous-isostatic
dynamic topography with the $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase.  In the
long-wave lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ so that
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

With the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $F(h)=0$, i.e.
$W(h)=0$, the same physics is written in the compact form

$$
\chi_{0}(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u},
\qquad e_{s}= \chi_{0}(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

which coincides with $\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ to $O(u)$
for $u\ll1$ and gives $\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, i.e.
$\chi_{0}\approx 1/2$ for $kh\sim O(1)$.  The $u\sinh u$ numerator
obtained by double counting the $2\mu w_{z}$ term after $w_{z}(0)=0$
gives the unphysical quadratic long-wave limit $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ and
is rejected on asymptotic grounds. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the harmonic mode the steady Stokes problem is
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\Big[\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,
\qquad P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] .
$$

On the material free surface the steady kinematic conditions are
$w(0)=0,\;u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e.

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

and hence $w_{,z}(0)=-k\Phi'(0)=0$ identically.  On the top

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu w_{,z}(0)=-P(0)
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,
$$

so with the buoyancy renormalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=2\mu k b,
\tag{1}
$$

for the admissible free solution

$$
\Phi(z)=b\,z\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz,\qquad c=-\frac{b}{k},
$$

which satisfies $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  The $2\mu w_{,z}$ viscous normal
stress is already zero by $u_{x}(0)=0$; it is not an independent
contribution at $z=0$.  Keeping it symbolically after $W'(0)=0$ has been
imposed is the source of the spurious $ \cosh^{2}u$ term that appears in
the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ algebra.

At the base the stated physical condition is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, not
$P(h)=0$.  With $w_{,z}=-k\Phi'$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\tag{2}
$$

i.e. $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$.  Eq.(2) is the only independent normal-stress
condition at $z=h$.  Imposing in addition $P(h)=0$ together with
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ over-constrains the biharmonic solution and is what
produces the extra $C_{h}^{2}$ in the denominator.

The remaining independent conditions are the shear and the normal
condition (2).  With $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$,

$$
\Phi'(h)=dkhC_{h}+(bh+d)S_{h},\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

gives

$$
b\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]=duC_{h},\qquad 
d=b\,\frac{C_{h}-uS_{h}}{uC_{h}} .
\tag{3}
$$

The basal shear is

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

and with (3)

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}\big].
$$

Eliminating $d$ with (3),

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\big[C_{h}+uS_{h}\big],
$$

so that, up to the usual $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$
phase,

$$
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\frac{1}{C_{h}+uS_{h}} .
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b
     =\frac{S_{0}}{C_{h}+uS_{h}}\,u,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad u=kh.
$$

This is the transfer function with the conventional impermeable-base
normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, $W(h)=0$, which removes the additive constant
in the biharmonic solution.  It has the required asymptotics

$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1,\qquad \chi(u)\to0,\;u\gg1,
$$

$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, and for $kh=O(1)$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad\chi_{0}\approx\frac12,
$$

the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography with the $\sin kx$
basal shear producing a $\cos kx$ surface deflection.  The long-wave
lubrication limit is $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho
g$, as expected for a finite thickness viscous sheet.

The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ form is obtained if the $2\mu w_{,z}$
term is kept symbolically in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu w_{,z}(0)$ after
$w_{,z}(0)=0$ has already been enforced by $u_{x}(0)=0$, and then
$P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ is used together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two
independent base conditions.  Once $W'(0)=0$ is enforced
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly and the extra $2\mu W'$ is already
absorbed; re-introducing it in the elimination produces the additional
$\cosh^{2}u$ denominator.  The two expressions coincide to $O(u)$ for
$u\ll1$, which is why the lubrication limit is the same in both camps.

The sinh-numerator $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ gives
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$, a quadratic long-wave limit inconsistent
with lubrication for a sheet of finite thickness, and can be discarded
on asymptotic grounds.  With the stated conditions
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ the compact
impermeable-base form $\chi=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ is the conventional
steady Stokes response to a harmonic basal shear and gives the usual
$O(1/2)$ viscous dynamic topography for $kh\sim O(1)$.

1.text:
With the harmonic mode

$$
\psi=F(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=F'\sin kx,\qquad w=-kF\cos kx,
\qquad D\equiv d/dz,
$$

$$
(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[F''+k^{2}F\big]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}\big[F'''-3k^{2}F'\big]\cos kx
       =-P-2\mu kF' ,
\qquad P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[F'''-k^{2}F'\big] .
$$

On the material steady top $w(0)=u_{x}(0)=0$

$$
F(0)=0,\qquad F'(0)=0,\qquad w_{z}(0)=-kF'(0)=0,
$$

so that up to an additive constant

$$
F(z)=b\,z\cosh kz+(c+d z)\sinh kz,\qquad b+kc=0 .
$$

Then $F'''(0)=2b k^{2}$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)\cos kx
            =2\mu k b\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyancy renormalisation $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx,
\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b, \tag{1}
$$

the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$ versus
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ being absorbed in the sign.  The viscous part
$2\mu w_{z}$ is identically zero at $z=0$ once $u_{x}(0)=0$ is imposed.

At the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu\big[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)\big]=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

Put $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$, $b=-kc$.  Then

$$
F'(h)=S_{h}(bu+d)+duC_{h},\qquad
F'''(h)=k^{2}\!\Big[\,2bC_{h}+buS_{h}+3dS_{h}+duC_{h}\Big],
$$

and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$$
b\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]=duC_{h},\qquad
d=b\,\frac{C_{h}-uS_{h}}{uC_{h}} .
$$

Hence

$$
F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k\Big[(bu+d)C_{h}+duS_{h}\Big]
       =2kb\,\frac{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{uC_{h}},
$$

so that from (2)

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\,\frac{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{uC_{h}},\qquad
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\,\frac{uC_{h}}{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}} .
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b
      =S_{0}\,\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},\qquad u=kh,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,
\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
      =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
$$

the sign being the usual $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$
shift.  In particular

$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1,\qquad
\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0,\;u\gg1,
$$

$$
\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47\quad{\rm at}\quad kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2,
$$

so that for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}\approx\frac12,
$$

the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography
$e_{s}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$ with the $90^{\circ}$ phase
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$.  In the lubrication
limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

With the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $F(h)=0$,
$W(h)=0$, the same solution is written in the compact form

$$
\chi_{0}(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u},\qquad 
e_{s}=\chi_{0}(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

$\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, which coincides with
$\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and gives the
same long-wave lubrication limit $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ numerator has the wrong
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ long-wave behaviour and is the result of double
counting the $2\mu w_{z}$ viscous normal stress after $w_{z}(0)=0$ has
already been imposed by $u_{x}(0)=0$.  Up to the conventional sign this
is the steady Stokes transfer for the four stated conditions
$F(0)=F'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, i.e. the $O(1/2)$ dynamic-topography
law normally quoted in the literature. ∎

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The bookkeeping of the normal stress at the material free surface is what decides the numerator. With the usual harmonic mode
$\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= [\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi']\cos kx
           =-P+2\mu w_{,z}$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.
The steady material surface is

$u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$,

hence
$w_{,z}(0)=-k\Phi'(0)=0$ identically. On the top

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,

the $2\mu w_{,z}$ viscous normal stress is already zero by the
kinematic condition $u_{x}(0)=0$. It should not be kept as an independent
contribution after $w_{,z}(0)=0$ has been imposed. With the usual
ansatz

$\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,

$\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2}$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx$.
With the buoyancy renormalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$,
$ b=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$,

and the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$ against
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ is absorbed in the sign.

At the base the physical condition is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,

$\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
i.e. $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$,
and the imposed shear

$\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.

Put $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$. With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\Phi'(h)=dkh\,C_{h}+(bh+d)S_{h}$,

$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives

$b\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]=duC_{h}$,

$d=b\,u^{-1}\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]/C_{h}$.

Hence

$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}]
     =2k b\,[C_{h}+uS_{h}]$.

The shear condition is therefore

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\,[C_{h}+uS_{h}]$,

so that with the conventional impermeable-base normalisation
$\Phi(h)=0$, $W(h)=0$, the additive constant in the biharmonic solution
is removed,

$b=\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\,\frac{1}{C_{h}+uS_{h}}$.

With $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{C_{h}+uS_{h}}\,u$,

i.e. in modulus with the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase absorbed,

$e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx$,

$\chi(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0$,
$u=kh$.

This is the steady Stokes transfer for the stated four conditions
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ with
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$.  In particular

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$, $u\ll1$, 
$\chi(u)\to0$ exponentially, $u\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$,

so that for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{0}\approx1/2$,

and the long-wave lubrication limit is the expected linear one

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

with the correct $90^{\circ}$ phase between basal shear $\sin kx$ and
topography $\cos kx$.

The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ forms quoted by Colleagues 1,3,5 are
obtained if the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term is kept symbolically in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu w_{,z}(0)$ after $w_{,z}(0)=0$ has already been
imposed by $u_{x}(0)=0$, and then $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ is used together
with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two independent conditions. Once
$W'(0)=0$ is enforced $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly and the extra
$2\mu W'$ is already absorbed; retaining it a second time in the
elimination produces the additional $\cosh^{2}u$ term in the denominator
and the $u\cosh u$ numerator. The two expressions coincide only to
$O(u)$ for $u\ll1$.

The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ sinh-numerator form gives
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$, a quadratic lubrication limit
inconsistent with the sheet lubrication expectation $\chi\sim u$, and
can be discarded on asymptotic grounds.  Colleague 2’s claim of
algebraic equivalence between $u\cosh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ and
$u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ is not exact; the forms agree only to
$O(u)$ in the long wave limit.  With the impermeable-base
normalisation the compact transfer function $\chi(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$
is the conventional viscous-isostatic response to $\tau_{b}=S_{0}\sin kx$
with the stated free-surface and base conditions.

public_text.4:
I think the point where the algebra splits is the handling of the viscous normal stress at the free surface and the way the base normal condition is used.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \Big[\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx
          =-P+2\mu w_{,z},
$$
$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],\qquad w_{,z}=-k\Phi'.
$$

On the material steady surface

$$
w(0)=0,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0 .
$$

Hence $w_{,z}(0)=0$ identically and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

The $2\mu w_{,z}$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ is already zero by $u_{x}(0)=0$; it should not be kept as an independent contribution after the kinematic condition is imposed. With the usual
$\Phi(z)=b z\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,

$$
\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx,
$$

so that with $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b ,\tag{1}
$$
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in the sign.

At the base the physical condition quoted is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\tag{2}
$$
and the imposed shear

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}. \tag{3}
$$

With $u=kh$, $C_{u}=\cosh u$, $S_{u}=\sinh u$,

$$
\Phi'(h)=d\,uC_{u}+(b u+d)S_{u},
$$

and (2) gives

$$
b\big[C_{u}-uS_{u}\big]=d\,uC_{u}. \tag{4}
$$

In the conventional biharmonic normalisation the base is impermeable,
$\Phi(h)=0$, so the additive constant in the $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$
solution is removed and (2) is the only independent normal-stress
condition at $z=h$, i.e. $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ is absorbed in (2).

Now

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)C_{u}+u d S_{u}\big].
$$

Eliminating $d$ with (4) in (3),

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\big[C_{u}+uS_{u}\big],
$$

so that

$$
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\frac{1}{C_{u}+uS_{u}}.
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b=\frac{S_{0}}{C_{u}+uS_{u}}\,
\frac{u}{u} ,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u},\qquad u=kh,
$$

the usual $90^{\circ}$ phase between $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ and
$e_{s}\propto\cos kx$. With the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ buoyancy
renormalisation this is the compact steady transfer function.

The asymptotics are the physically expected ones:

$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1,\qquad
\chi(u)\to0\;{\rm exponentially},\;u\gg1,
$$

$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, and for $kh=O(1)$
$e_{s}\simeq\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar order-unity
viscous-isostatic dynamic topography with linear lubrication limit
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Retaining the $2\mu w_{,z}$ term symbolically in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu
w_{,z}(0)$ after $w_{,z}(0)=0$ has already been imposed by $u_{x}(0)=0$, and
then using $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two
independent conditions, produces the extra $\cosh^{2}u$ in the denominator
and the $u\cosh u$ numerator. Once $W'(0)=0$ is enforced,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly and the $2\mu W'$ contribution is already
absorbed; keeping it a second time in the elimination is the double
counting noted by 4 and 7. The two forms coincide to $O(u)$ in the long
wave limit, which is why the lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ is common to
both camps, but the impermeable-base normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e.
$W(h)=0$, gives the clean denominator $\cosh u+u\sinh u$ and the
conventional $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ screening.

The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ sinh-numerator that appeared in an
earlier round has the wrong long-wave $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ and is
inconsistent with the lubrication expectation. With the bookkeeping above
the steady response is the compact form $\chi=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$,
with the $90^{\circ}$ phase and the familiar $O(1/2)$ value for $kh\sim1$.

The steady harmonic Stokes field can be written with

$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$, $D=d/dz$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu [F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$, 
$P=-(\mu/k)[F'''-k^{2}F']$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-P-2\mu kF'=
(\mu/k)[F'''-3k^{2}F']\cos kx$.

On the material free surface in the quasi–static limit

$u_{x}(0)=0,\;w(0)=0\iff F(0)=0,\;F'(0)=0$,

and with an inessential additive constant

$F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,

so that $w_{z}(0)=-kF'(0)=0$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)\cos kx$.
Now $F'''(0)=2k^{2}b$ and with the buoyancy
normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

\begin{equation*}
\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}F'''(0)=2\mu k b,\qquad
b=\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k},
\end{equation*}
the $90^{\circ}$ phase $ \tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$, $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$
being absorbed in the sign.

At $z=h$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ ,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff \mu[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)]=S_{0}$ .

Put $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$.  With $c=-b/k$,

$F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ gives

$b\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]=duC_{h}$, 
$d=b\,\dfrac{C_{h}-uS_{h}}{uC_{h}}$,

and

$F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}\big]$.

Eliminating $d$,
$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\,\frac{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}}{uC_{h}},
\qquad
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\frac{uC_{h}}{u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}} .
$$

Hence on the steady branch

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b
 =S_{0}\,\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},
\qquad u=kh,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
 =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0 ,
$$

the sign being the usual $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$  $90^{\circ}$
phase shift.  In particular

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1$, 
$\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0,\;u\gg1$,

$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45$–$0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0$–$1.2$.  For the
geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi_{0}\approx\frac12,
$$

the familiar $e_{s}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$ viscous-isostatic
dynamic topography with the $\sin kx\to\cos kx$ phase.  In the
long-wave lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ so that
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

With the conventional impermeable-base normalisation $F(h)=0$, i.e.
$W(h)=0$, the same physics is written in the compact form

$$
\chi_{0}(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u},
\qquad e_{s}= \chi_{0}(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

which coincides with $\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ to $O(u)$
for $u\ll1$ and gives $\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, i.e.

obtained by double counting the $2\mu w_{z}$ term after $w_{z}(0)=0$
gives the unphysical quadratic long-wave limit $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ and
is rejected on asymptotic grounds. ∎
public_text.7:
With the harmonic mode the steady Stokes problem is
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}=\Big[\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,
\qquad P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] .
$$

On the material free surface the steady kinematic conditions are
$w(0)=0,\;u_{x}(0)=0$, i.e.

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

and hence $w_{,z}(0)=-k\Phi'(0)=0$ identically.  On the top

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu w_{,z}(0)=-P(0)
          =\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,
$$

so with the buoyancy renormalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}= \frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=2\mu k b,
\tag{1}
$$

for the admissible free solution

$$
\Phi(z)=b\,z\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz,\qquad c=-\frac{b}{k},
$$

which satisfies $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$.  The $2\mu w_{,z}$ viscous normal
stress is already zero by $u_{x}(0)=0$; it is not an independent
contribution at $z=0$.  Keeping it symbolically after $W'(0)=0$ has been
imposed is the source of the spurious $ \cosh^{2}u$ term that appears in
the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ algebra.

At the base the stated physical condition is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, not
$P(h)=0$.  With $w_{,z}=-k\Phi'$,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0
\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\tag{2}
$$

i.e. $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$.  Eq.(2) is the only independent normal-stress
condition at $z=h$.  Imposing in addition $P(h)=0$ together with
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ over-constrains the biharmonic solution and is what
produces the extra $C_{h}^{2}$ in the denominator.

The remaining independent conditions are the shear and the normal
condition (2).  With $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$,

$$
\Phi'(h)=dkhC_{h}+(bh+d)S_{h},\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)
$$

gives

$$
b\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]=duC_{h},\qquad 
d=b\,\frac{C_{h}-uS_{h}}{uC_{h}} .
\tag{3}
$$

The basal shear is

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

and with (3)

$$
\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k\big[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}\big].
$$

Eliminating $d$ with (3),

$$
\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\big[C_{h}+uS_{h}\big],
$$

so that, up to the usual $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ $90^{\circ}$
phase,

$$
b=\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\frac{1}{C_{h}+uS_{h}} .
$$

With (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b
     =\frac{S_{0}}{C_{h}+uS_{h}}\,u,
$$

i.e. in modulus

$$
e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx,\qquad
\chi(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad u=kh.
$$

This is the transfer function with the conventional impermeable-base
normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, $W(h)=0$, which removes the additive constant
in the biharmonic solution.  It has the required asymptotics

$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\;u\ll1,\qquad \chi(u)\to0,\;u\gg1,
$$

$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, and for $kh=O(1)$

$$
e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad\chi_{0}\approx\frac12,
$$

the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography with the $\sin kx$
basal shear producing a $\cos kx$ surface deflection.  The long-wave
lubrication limit is $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho
g$, as expected for a finite thickness viscous sheet.

The $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ form is obtained if the $2\mu w_{,z}$
term is kept symbolically in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu w_{,z}(0)$ after
$w_{,z}(0)=0$ has already been enforced by $u_{x}(0)=0$, and then
$P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$ is used together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two
independent base conditions.  Once $W'(0)=0$ is enforced
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly and the extra $2\mu W'$ is already
absorbed; re-introducing it in the elimination produces the additional
$\cosh^{2}u$ denominator.  The two expressions coincide to $O(u)$ for
$u\ll1$, which is why the lubrication limit is the same in both camps.

The sinh-numerator $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ gives
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$, a quadratic long-wave limit inconsistent
with lubrication for a sheet of finite thickness, and can be discarded
on asymptotic grounds.  With the stated conditions
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ the compact
impermeable-base form $\chi=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ is the conventional
steady Stokes response to a harmonic basal shear and gives the usual
$O(1/2)$ viscous dynamic topography for $kh\sim O(1)$.

The bookkeeping of the normal stress at the material free surface is what decides the numerator. With the usual harmonic mode
$\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= [\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi']\cos kx
           =-P+2\mu w_{,z}$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.
The steady material surface is

$u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=0\iff \Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$,

hence
$w_{,z}(0)=-k\Phi'(0)=0$ identically. On the top

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$,

the $2\mu w_{,z}$ viscous normal stress is already zero by the
kinematic condition $u_{x}(0)=0$. It should not be kept as an independent
contribution after $w_{,z}(0)=0$ has been imposed. With the usual
ansatz

$\Phi(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,

$\Phi'''(0)=2bk^{2}$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx$.
With the buoyancy renormalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$,
$ b=\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k$,

and the $90^{\circ}$ phase $e_{s}\propto\cos kx$ against
$\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$ is absorbed in the sign.

At the base the physical condition is $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,

$\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(h)-3\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
i.e. $P(h)=2\mu w_{,z}(h)$,
and the imposed shear

$\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.

Put $u=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$. With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\Phi'(h)=dkh\,C_{h}+(bh+d)S_{h}$,

$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ gives

$b\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]=duC_{h}$,

$d=b\,u^{-1}\big[C_{h}-uS_{h}\big]/C_{h}$.

Hence

$\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)=2k[(d+bu)C_{h}+udS_{h}]
     =2k b\,[C_{h}+uS_{h}]$.

The shear condition is therefore

$\frac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2k b\,[C_{h}+uS_{h}]$,

so that with the conventional impermeable-base normalisation
$\Phi(h)=0$, $W(h)=0$, the additive constant in the biharmonic solution
is removed,

$b=\frac{S_{0}}{2k\mu}\,\frac{1}{C_{h}+uS_{h}}$.

With $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k b$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{C_{h}+uS_{h}}\,u$,

i.e. in modulus with the $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase absorbed,

$e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx$,

$\chi(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0$,
$u=kh$.

This is the steady Stokes transfer for the stated four conditions
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ with
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$.  In particular

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$, $u\ll1$, 
$\chi(u)\to0$ exponentially, $u\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$,

so that for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{0}\approx1/2$,

and the long-wave lubrication limit is the expected linear one

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

with the correct $90^{\circ}$ phase between basal shear $\sin kx$ and

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The steady harmonic Stokes problem is
$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$
with $D=d/dz$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[F'''-3k^{2}F']\cos kx=-P-2\mu kF'$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$.

Steady material top $u_x(0)=0$ gives $F'(0)=0$ and in the steady limit
$w(0)=0$ gives $F(0)=0$. Hence $w_z(0)=-kF'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$.
With $F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $b+kc=0$, $F'''(0)=2bk^{2}$,
so

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx$.
With the buoyancy renormalisation $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k b$,
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in the sign.
The $2\mu w_z$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ is identically zero at $z=0$ once
$F'(0)=0$ is imposed, i.e. $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly.

Base conditions stated are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$,
$\mu[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)]=S_0$.

Put $u=kh$, $C_h=\cosh u$, $S_h=\sinh u$, $c=-b/k$. Then
$F'(h)=S_h(bu+d)+duC_h$ and $F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ gives
$b[C_h-uS_h]=duC_h$, $d=b(C_h-uS_h)/uC_h$.
Hence

$F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k[(bu+d)C_h+udS_h]=2kb\,[u^{2}+C_h^{2}]/uC_h$,

so that

$S_0/\mu=2kb\,[u^{2}+C_h^{2}]/uC_h$,
$b=S_0/(2k\mu)\,uC_h/[u^{2}+C_h^{2}]$.

With $\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k b$,

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$,
$u=kh$,

i.e. in modulus

$e_s(x)=\chi(u)S_0/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$,
$\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]
=[u/\cosh u+\cosh u/u]^{-1}>0$.

Asymptotics $\chi=u+O(u^{3})$, $u\ll1$, $\chi\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$, $u\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$, and for the
geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$ $\chi\approx1/2$, the familiar
$e_s\simeq S_0/2\Delta\rho g$ dynamic topography with the $\sin$ basal
shear $\to\cos$ topography phase. Long wave lubrication limit
$\chi\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

The compact form $\chi_0(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ quoted by Colleagues 4,6,7
is the same physics with the conventional impermeable-base normalisation
$F(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$, imposed in addition to the four stated
conditions. With $F(h)=0$ the elimination gives
$S_0/\mu=2kb[C_h+uS_h]$ and $\chi_0=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$,
$\chi_0^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, coinciding with the above
$\chi$ to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and giving the same lubrication limit
$\chi\simeq kh$. The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ sinh-numerator
form gives $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$ and is ruled out by lubrication.

The disagreement in the round is the bookkeeping of $2\mu w_z$ after
$w_z(0)=0$ is already enforced by $u_x(0)=0$. Retaining $2\mu w_z$
symbolically in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)+2\mu w_z(0)$ after $w_z(0)=0$ and
then using $P(h)=2\mu w_z(h)$ together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two
independent base conditions produces the extra $\cosh^{2}u$ term and the
$u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ vs $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ discrepancy.
With the conditions as stated, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, the
consistent transfer is $\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$, up to the
conventional $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ renormalisation and the
$90^{\circ}$ phase. The $ \approx 1/2$ $O(1)$ value for $kh\sim O(1)$
is robust to the normalisation.

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$ for $u\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$, and
$\chi\approx1/2$ for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$,
the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography
$e_{s}\simeq\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$
phase.  Long wave lubrication: $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The compact form $\chi_{0}(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ quoted by Colleagues
4,6,7 is the same physics with the conventional impermeable-base
normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$, imposed in addition to the four
conditions stated in the problem.  With $\Phi(h)=0$ the algebra gives

$\chi_{0}(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$, $\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at
$kh\simeq0.8$, which coincides with $\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$
to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and gives the same long-wave limit
$\chi\simeq kh$.  The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ numerator gives
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$ and is ruled out by the lubrication
requirement $e_{s}\sim kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The $2\mu w_{z}$ part of
$\sigma_{zz}$ vanishes at $z=0$ once $u_{x}(0)=0$ is imposed; keeping it
symbolically after $w_{z}(0)=0$ and then using $P(h)=2\mu w_{z}(h)$
together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two independent base conditions is
the double counting noted in the discussion.  With the four conditions
as written the steady Stokes transfer is the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$
form, $O(1/2)$ for $kh\sim O(1)$, i.e. essentially the conventional

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes mode can be written with a stream
function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$,
$u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.
With the Stokes sign convention
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.
On a material steady free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$ gives
$\Phi'(0)=0$ and $w_{z}(0)=0$, so that the viscous part of $\sigma_{zz}$
vanishes at $z=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.
With the buoyancy renormalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$,
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in the sign.

With the four conditions quoted in the problem,
$\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$,
the admissible free solution can be written as
$\Phi(z)=A(1+kz)\cosh kz+(-A+Dz)\sinh kz$, $A\neq0$, $D$ free.
Putting $u=kh$, $C_{u}=\cosh u$, $S_{u}=\sinh u$ the base normal stress gives
$A=d h$ after elimination of the $D$ constant and the shear condition gives

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2kA\,\dfrac{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}{uC_{u}}$,
$A=\dfrac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\dfrac{uC_{u}}{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}$.

Since $\Phi'''(0)=2Ak^{3}$,
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=2\mu kA$
so that in modulus

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}$,
$e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx$,

$\chi(u)=\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
      =\Big[\dfrac{u}{\cosh u}+\dfrac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0$,
$u=kh$.
Hence $\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$
for $u\gg1$, with $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$.
For the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{0}\approx1/2$,

the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography $e_{s}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$
with the usual $\sin kx$ basal shear $\to\cos kx$ topography phase.
In the long-wave lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Colleagues 1,2,3,5 obtain this $u\cosh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ transfer
under the four stated conditions $\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$.
Colleagues 4,7 quote the compact form
$\chi_{0}(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$,
$e_{s}=\chi_{0}(u)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
This is the same physics with the conventional impermeable-base
normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$, imposed in addition to
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. With the problem as stated $\Phi(h)=0$ is not required
and the $u\cosh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ form is the direct Stokes solution
of the four stated conditions. The two forms coincide to $O(u)$ for
$u\ll1$ and both give the correct lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and
the $O(1/2)$ value for $kh\sim1$.

The $u\sinh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ numerator quoted by Colleague 6 gives
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$, i.e. the wrong quadratic long-wave
lubrication scaling, and is ruled out. The difference between the
$u\cosh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ and the compact $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$
forms is the double counting of the $2\mu w_{z}$ viscous normal stress
after $w_{z}(0)=0$ has already been enforced by $u_{x}(0)=0$. Once
$W'(0)=0$ is enforced $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly and the extra
$2\mu W'$ is already absorbed; re-introducing it in the elimination
produces the additional $\cosh^{2}u$ denominator. The $90^{\circ}$ phase,
the $\Delta\rho$ buoyancy renormalisation and the $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
scaling are robust. ∎

reflection_text.5:
The harmonic sin kx mode is
ψ=F(z) sin kx, u_x=F' sin kx, w=-kF cos kx, (D²-k²)²F=0,
σ_xz=μ[F''+k²F] sin kx,
σ_zz= μk⁻¹[F'''-3k²F'] cos kx = -P-2μkF', P=-μk⁻¹[F'''-k²F'].
On the steady material top the stated conditions are u_x(0)=0 and
σ_zz(0)=Δρ g e cos kx.  With the inessential additive constant removed
F(0)=F'(0)=0 gives w_z(0)=-kF'(0)=0 so that σ_zz(0)=-P(0)=μk⁻¹F'''(0)
exactly; the 2μw_z piece is identically zero once u_x(0)=0 is imposed.
With F(z)=(a+bz)cosh kz+(c+dz)sinh kz, a=0, b+kc=0,
F(z)=bz cosh kz+(c+dz)sinh kz, c=-b/k,
F'''(0)=2k²b and
σ_zz(0)=2μk b cos kx.
Hence on the steady branch with the buoyancy renormalisation ρ→Δρ
Δρ g e_s =2μk b, the 90° phase e_s∝cos kx, τ_b∝sin kx being absorbed in sign.

Base:
σ_zz(h)=0 ⇔ F'''(h)=3k²F'(h),
σ_xz(h)=S0 ⇔ μ[F''(h)+k²F(h)]=S0.
Put u=kh, C_h=cosh u, S_h=sinh u.
F'''(h)=3k²F'(h) gives b[C_h-uS_h]=duC_h,
d=b(C_h-uS_h)/(uC_h).
Then
F''(h)+k²F(h)=2k[(bu+d)C_h+udS_h]=2kb (u²+C_h²)/(uC_h).
Hence
S0/μ=2k b (u²+C_h²)/(uC_h),
b=S0/(2μk) · uC_h/(u²+C_h²),
Δρ g e_s=2μk b=S0·uC_h/(u²+C_h²).

In modulus
e_s=χ(u)S0/Δρ g,
χ(u)=u cosh u/[u²+cosh²u]=[u/cosh u+cosh u/u]⁻¹>0,
u=kh.
Asymptotics χ=u+O(u³) for u≪1, χ∼2u e⁻ᵘ→0 for u≫1,
χ_max≈0.45–0.47 at kh≈1.0–1.2, so for the geologically relevant kh=O(1)
χ₀≈½, e_s≈½S0/Δρ g, with the familiar sin→cos 90° phase and the
lubrication limit e_s≈kh S0/Δρ g.

The conventional impermeable-base normalisation Φ(h)=0, W(h)=0 i.e.
F(h)=0 removes the additive constant in the biharmonic solution and is
the form most often quoted in the literature.  With that extra
normalisation the elimination gives
b=S0/(2kμ)[cosh u+u sinh u]⁻¹,
Δρ g e_s=S0 u/[cosh u+u sinh u],
χ₀(u)=u/[cosh u+u sinh u]=u cosh u/[u²+cosh²u] to O(u) for u≪1,
χ₀_max≈0.39 at kh≈0.8, χ₀≈u for u≪1, and χ₀≈½ for kh∼O(1).
The two forms coincide in the lubrication limit; the difference is
precisely the extra Φ(h)=0/W(h)=0 condition not stated in the problem
statement.  Keeping the 2μw_z term symbolically in σ_zz(0)=-P+2μw_z
after w_z(0)=0 has already been imposed by u_x(0)=0 is the double
counting that produces the extra cosh² term and the alternative
numerators.  The sinh-numerator χ_s=u sinh u/[u²+cosh²u] gives
χ_s≈u²/2 for u≪1, a quadratic long-wave limit inconsistent with the
sheet lubrication expectation χ∼u, and is rejected.

Unresolved: the problem as written does not impose w(h)=0/Φ(h)=0,
so the literal four-condition solution is χ=u cosh u/[u²+cosh²u].
If the conventional impermeable base is adopted the compact quoted
form is χ₀=u/[cosh u+u sinh u]≈½ for kh∼1.  Both reduce to the
familiar O(½) viscous-isostatic dynamic topography e_s≈S0/2Δρ g with
the 90° sin→cos phase.

$\psi=F(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=F'\sin kx$, $w=-kF\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}F=0$
with $D=d/dz$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[F''+k^{2}F]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[F'''-3k^{2}F']\cos kx=-P-2\mu kF'$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[F'''-k^{2}F']$.

Steady material top $u_x(0)=0$ gives $F'(0)=0$ and in the steady limit
$w(0)=0$ gives $F(0)=0$. Hence $w_z(0)=-kF'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)\cos kx$.
With $F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $b+kc=0$, $F'''(0)=2bk^{2}$,
so

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx$.
With the buoyancy renormalisation $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k b$,
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in the sign.
The $2\mu w_z$ part of $\sigma_{zz}$ is identically zero at $z=0$ once
$F'(0)=0$ is imposed, i.e. $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly.

Base conditions stated are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$,

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$,
$\mu[F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)]=S_0$.

Put $u=kh$, $C_h=\cosh u$, $S_h=\sinh u$, $c=-b/k$. Then
$F'(h)=S_h(bu+d)+duC_h$ and $F'''(h)=3k^{2}F'(h)$ gives
$b[C_h-uS_h]=duC_h$, $d=b(C_h-uS_h)/uC_h$.
Hence

$F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k[(bu+d)C_h+udS_h]=2kb\,[u^{2}+C_h^{2}]/uC_h$,

so that

$S_0/\mu=2kb\,[u^{2}+C_h^{2}]/uC_h$,
$b=S_0/(2k\mu)\,uC_h/[u^{2}+C_h^{2}]$.

With $\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k b$,

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$,
$u=kh$,

i.e. in modulus

$e_s(x)=\chi(u)S_0/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$,
$\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]
=[u/\cosh u+\cosh u/u]^{-1}>0$.

Asymptotics $\chi=u+O(u^{3})$, $u\ll1$, $\chi\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$, $u\gg1$,

shear $\to\cos$ topography phase. Long wave lubrication limit
$\chi\simeq kh$, $e_s\simeq kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

The compact form $\chi_0(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ quoted by Colleagues 4,6,7
is the same physics with the conventional impermeable-base normalisation
$F(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$, imposed in addition to the four stated
conditions. With $F(h)=0$ the elimination gives
$S_0/\mu=2kb[C_h+uS_h]$ and $\chi_0=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$,
$\chi_0^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at $kh\simeq0.8$, coinciding with the above
$\chi$ to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and giving the same lubrication limit
$\chi\simeq kh$. The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ sinh-numerator
form gives $\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$ and is ruled out by lubrication.

The disagreement in the round is the bookkeeping of $2\mu w_z$ after

After round 4 the algebra is settled to the four stated boundary conditions

* top $z=0$: $u_{x}=0$, $w=0$ in the steady limit $\;\Longleftrightarrow\;$ $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
  $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
* base $z=h$: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
  $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]=S_{0}$,

with $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $w=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx=-P-2\mu k\Phi'$.

With $F(0)=F'(0)=0$

$F(z)=bz\cosh kz+(c+dz)\sinh kz$, $c=-b/k$,

$F'''(0)=2bk^{2}$, $w_{z}(0)=-kF'(0)=0$, so that

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}F'''(0)=2\mu k b\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b$, the $90^{\circ}$ $\tau_{b}\propto\sin kx$,
$e_{s}\propto\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in the sign.  Put $u=kh$,
$C_{h}=\cosh u$, $S_{h}=\sinh u$.

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $b[C_{h}-uS_{h}]=duC_{h}$, $d=b(C_{h}-uS_{h})/uC_{h}$,
and

$F''(h)+k^{2}F(h)=2k[(bu+d)C_{h}+duS_{h}]
                =2kb\,[u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}]/uC_{h}$.

Hence

$S_{0}/\mu=2kb\,[u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}]/uC_{h}$,

$b=S_{0}/2\mu k\;uC_{h}/[u^{2}+C_{h}^{2}]$,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k b=S_{0}\,u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$.

In modulus

$e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g\cos kx$,

$\chi(u)=\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\dfrac{u}{\cosh u}+\dfrac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0$, $u=kh$,

$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$ for $u\gg1$,
$\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$, and
$\chi\approx1/2$ for the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$,
the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography
$e_{s}\simeq\frac12 S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $\sin\leftrightarrow\cos$
phase.  Long wave lubrication: $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The compact form $\chi_{0}(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ quoted by Colleagues
4,6,7 is the same physics with the conventional impermeable-base
normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$, imposed in addition to the four
conditions stated in the problem.  With $\Phi(h)=0$ the algebra gives

$\chi_{0}(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$, $\chi_{0}^{\max}\simeq0.39$ at
$kh\simeq0.8$, which coincides with $\chi(u)=u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$
to $O(u)$ for $u\ll1$ and gives the same long-wave limit
$\chi\simeq kh$.  The $u\sinh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$ numerator gives
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$ and is ruled out by the lubrication
requirement $e_{s}\sim kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The $2\mu w_{z}$ part of
$\sigma_{zz}$ vanishes at $z=0$ once $u_{x}(0)=0$ is imposed; keeping it
symbolically after $w_{z}(0)=0$ and then using $P(h)=2\mu w_{z}(h)$
together with $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ as two independent base conditions is
the double counting noted in the discussion.  With the four conditions
as written the steady Stokes transfer is the $u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$
form, $O(1/2)$ for $kh\sim O(1)$, i.e. essentially the conventional
$ e_{s}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$ dynamic topography. ∎
reflection_text.2:
The harmonic Stokes mode can be written with a stream
function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$,
$u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $(D^{2}-k^{2})^{2}\Phi=0$.
With the Stokes sign convention
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.
On a material steady free surface $u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=0$ gives
$\Phi'(0)=0$ and $w_{z}(0)=0$, so that the viscous part of $\sigma_{zz}$
vanishes at $z=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.
With the buoyancy renormalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$,
the $90^{\circ}$ $\sin kx\leftrightarrow\cos kx$ phase being absorbed in the sign.

With the four conditions quoted in the problem,
$\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx$,
the admissible free solution can be written as
$\Phi(z)=A(1+kz)\cosh kz+(-A+Dz)\sinh kz$, $A\neq0$, $D$ free.
Putting $u=kh$, $C_{u}=\cosh u$, $S_{u}=\sinh u$ the base normal stress gives
$A=d h$ after elimination of the $D$ constant and the shear condition gives

$\dfrac{S_{0}}{\mu}=2kA\,\dfrac{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}{uC_{u}}$,
$A=\dfrac{S_{0}}{2\mu k}\dfrac{uC_{u}}{u^{2}+C_{u}^{2}}$.

Since $\Phi'''(0)=2Ak^{3}$,
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}= \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=2\mu kA$
so that in modulus

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}$,
$e_{s}(x)=\chi(u)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\cos kx$,

$\chi(u)=\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
      =\Big[\dfrac{u}{\cosh u}+\dfrac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0$,
$u=kh$.
Hence $\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$, $\chi(u)\sim2u e^{-u}\to0$
for $u\gg1$, with $\chi_{\max}\simeq0.45\!-\!0.47$ at $kh\simeq1.0\!-\!1.2$.
For the geologically relevant $kh=O(1)$

$e_{s}\simeq\chi_{0}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{0}\approx1/2$,

the familiar viscous-isostatic dynamic topography $e_{s}\approx S_{0}/2\Delta\rho g$
with the usual $\sin kx$ basal shear $\to\cos kx$ topography phase.
In the long-wave lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Colleagues 1,2,3,5 obtain this $u\cosh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ transfer
under the four stated conditions $\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$.
Colleagues 4,7 quote the compact form
$\chi_{0}(u)=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$,
$e_{s}=\chi_{0}(u)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
This is the same physics with the conventional impermeable-base
normalisation $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$, imposed in addition to
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$. With the problem as stated $\Phi(h)=0$ is not required
and the $u\cosh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ form is the direct Stokes solution
of the four stated conditions. The two forms coincide to $O(u)$ for
$u\ll1$ and both give the correct lubrication limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and
the $O(1/2)$ value for $kh\sim1$.

The $u\sinh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ numerator quoted by Colleague 6 gives
$\chi\sim u^{2}/2$ for $u\ll1$, i.e. the wrong quadratic long-wave
lubrication scaling, and is ruled out. The difference between the
$u\cosh u/(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)$ and the compact $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$
forms is the double counting of the $2\mu w_{z}$ viscous normal stress
after $w_{z}(0)=0$ has already been enforced by $u_{x}(0)=0$. Once
$W'(0)=0$ is enforced $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)$ exactly and the extra
$2\mu W'$ is already absorbed; re-introducing it in the elimination
produces the additional $\cosh^{2}u$ denominator. The $90^{\circ}$ phase,
the $\Delta\rho$ buoyancy renormalisation and the $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
scaling are robust. ∎
